items.title: Lagos dismisses N700m billboard fee claim
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has dismissed claims circulating on social media that it increased billboard permit fees in the state to N700 million, describing the allegation as false and politically motivated. The clarification follows allegations by opposition parties over an alleged increase in fees for billboard permits in Lagos, which they linked to the low visibility of some political campaign materials along major roads in the state. In a statement on Sunday, the Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Gbenga Omotoso, said the state government neither owned nor operated billboards, explaining that outdoor advertising structures were controlled by private operators. According to him, the most expensive commercial billboard in the state costs approximately N10 million monthly, with rates determined entirely by private owners rather than the government. “The Lagos State Signage and Advertisement Agency (LASAA) is only a regulator, not an operator,” Omotoso said, adding that the state remained committed to providing equal opportunities for all political parties and candidates. Urging critics and political actors to comply with established regulations rather than spread misinformation, the commissioner outlined the statutory requirements governing outdoor advertising in the state. He said prospective outdoor advertising practitioners were required to pay a one-off, non-refundable registration fee of N7 million to LASAA, register with the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) and meet other legal requirements. Omotoso explained that all advertisements, including political campaign materials, could only be displayed on approved structures managed by registered practitioners with valid LASAA permits. He added that such structures must comply with strict location, structural safety and environmental standards. The commissioner further clarified that statutory permit fees paid by billboard owners to LASAA were different from commercial production and media placement charges. He said regulatory rates were determined by the size, format and designated zone of the advertising structure. Omotoso also disclosed that LASAA had recently conducted public sensitisation sessions to educate political parties, candidates and advertising practitioners on regulations governing election campaign advertisements. He added that the agency would remove all campaign materials after the conclusion of election activities at no cost to the public as part of efforts to restore the state’s visual aesthetics. The post Lagos dismisses N700m billboard fee claim appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lagos prosperity driven by public servants’ dedication — Hamzat
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, has attributed the state’s economic prosperity and development to the dedication, professionalism and contributions of its public servants. Hamzat spoke on Saturday while leading more than 4,000 civil and public servants in a fitness walk organised by the Lagos State Government as part of activities marking the 2026 Public Service Week. The exercise, which began at the Adeyemi Bero Auditorium, Alausa, Ikeja, featured aerobics and a brisk walk through Alausa and adjoining communities, promoting physical fitness, healthy living and workplace wellness among public sector employees. The deputy governor was accompanied by the Head of Service, Mr. Bode Agoro, and the Principal Secretary to President Bola Tinubu and former Lagos State Head of Service, Mr. Hakeem Muri-Okunola. Also in attendance were members of the Body of Permanent Secretaries, heads of extra-ministerial departments and offices, as well as civil and public servants from the mainstream public service, commissions and local governments across the state. Participants commenced the exercise with aerobics sessions before embarking on the fitness walk around the Alausa-Ikeja communities. Addressing the participants, Hamzat commended the workers for their impressive turnout, stressing the need for public servants to prioritise their health and wellbeing. He said the exercise reflected the health and dignity component of his PROMISE campaign, particularly the first pillar, People First agenda. “They say health is wealth. So, a healthy Lagos is a wealthy Lagos, and you are an important part of that promise,” he said. The deputy governor also acknowledged the strategic role of the public service in implementing government policies and programmes, describing the civil service as the machinery of government. According to him, without a functional and effective civil service, government activities and development initiatives would suffer. “Without a functional and effective civil service, nothing gets done,” Hamzat said, urging public servants to take pride in their contributions to governance. He noted that public servants were responsible for documenting government decisions and ensuring their implementation. Making reference to the ongoing electioneering period, Hamzat also responded to comments made during a political debate the previous day, where the civil service was reportedly identified as one of the challenges confronting Lagos State. He disagreed with the assessment, insisting that public servants remained indispensable to the delivery of government policies and development programmes. Hamzat further stressed the need to extend the benefits of economic prosperity to more households and businesses across the state. Earlier, Agoro disclosed that the exercise attracted more than 4,000 participants, expressing optimism that subsequent editions scheduled for January and February would record even greater participation. He commended the commitment of the workforce and reiterated the importance of collective involvement in activities that promote staff wellbeing. Also speaking, Muri-Okunola described public servants as key implementers of government policies and programmes. He commended their contributions to Lagos State’s development and urged them to sustain their commitment to effective service delivery. The fitness walk formed part of activities lined up by the Lagos State Government to promote a healthier workforce, strengthen camaraderie among public servants and reinforce the importance of staff wellbeing in effective service delivery. The post Lagos prosperity driven by public servants’ dedication — Hamzat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Aéroport international Ahmed Sékou Touré : la SOGEAG célèbre l’hospitalité et récompense ses passagers
items.description: L’aéroport international Ahmed Sékou Touré a vibré ce vendredi 13 novembre au rythme d’une cérémonie chaleureuse marquée par la convivialité et le partage. Organisé par la Société Guinéenne d’Exploitation des Aéroports de Guinée (SOGEAG), cet événement s’inscrit dans le cadre de la Semaine de l’hospitalité, qui se tient du 9 au 15 novembre 2026 sous le thème évocateur : « L’humain au cœur de l’expérience client ». Tout au long de cette semaine dédiée à l'amélioration de l'accueil et du confort des voyageurs, plusieurs initiatives de proximité ont été déployées au sein de la plateforme aéroportuaire. Parmi les actions phares ayant marqué les esprits figure la distribution gracieuse de collations et de repas aux passagers des différentes compagnies aériennes opérant depuis Conakry, une attention particulièrement saluée par les usagers en transit ou au départ. Le point d'orgue de cette cérémonie a été la remise de billets d’avion à d’heureux voyageurs tirés au sort. Le premier lauréat, Aly Badara Samb, ancien gouverneur de Saint-Louis, s’est vu décerner un billet aller-retour Conakry-Dakar-Conakry offert par la compagnie Mauritania Airlines. Très ému, il a salué cette initiative qui dépasse le simple cadre commercial pour incarner les valeurs de fraternité sous-régionale : « C’est d’abord avec surprise que j’ai appris cette nouvelle, et surtout avec un plaisir très fort de vous retrouver. Quand vous parlez d’hospitalité à un Sénégalais, c’est dans notre ADN, c’est ce que l’on appelle la teranga. Mais cette teranga n’est pas seulement sénégalaise ; elle est mauritanienne, elle est malienne, et elle est aussi profondément guinéenne . » Evoquant l’intégration africaine et les perspectives économiques portées par le programme Simandou 2040, l’ancien gouverneur a souligné l'importance de ces ponts aériens : « Nos pays sont tellement imbriqués que personne ne peut vivre en marge de ces frontières. C’est avec une immense fierté que j’accueille ce prix en République de Guinée. Vive la Guinée, vive le Sénégal, vive le Mali, la Mauritanie, et vive l’Afrique ! » Même enthousiasme du côté d’Aïssatou Sy, deuxième heureuse gagnante de la journée, qui a remporté un billet aller-retour Conakry-Dakar-Conakry offert cette fois par la compagnie Air Sénégal. Ravie de cette récompense inattendue, la passagère a exprimé sa profonde gratitude envers la SOGEAG et la compagnie nationale sénégalaise pour cette attention délicate qui transforme le voyage en une expérience mémorable et humaine. Prenant la parole au nom de la compagnie donatrice, Penda Fall, représentante et cheffe d’escale d’Air Sénégal en Guinée, a tenu à saluer le partenariat exemplaire avec la SOGEAG ainsi que la légendaire hospitalité guinéenne : « Je suis honorée par cette distinction faite à Air Sénégal. Au début, je venais en Guinée comme en aventure, mais aujourd’hui je suis complètement intégrée. On m’a ouvert toutes les portes et l’accueil chaleureux que m’a réservé ce peuple intègre fait que je me proclame désormais sénégalo-guinéenne. » Souhaitant plein succès aux futures initiatives de la plateforme aéroportuaire, elle a conclu en appelant de ses vœux la pérennisation de cet événement : « Vivement que cette collaboration continue d’aller de l’avant et que nous ayons des éditions à n’en plus finir. » A travers cette célébration réussie, la SOGEAG confirme sa volonté de hisser l’aéroport international Ahmed Sékou Touré aux meilleurs standards internationaux, non seulement par la modernisation de ses infrastructures, mais aussi par la qualité humaine de son accueil.

items.title: Sanusi, Ladoja warn against politicising traditional institutions
items.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful coexistence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning against the politicisation of traditional institutions. The two traditional rulers spoke on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, where they stressed the need for traditional institutions to remain above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national unity. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic, religious and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as one of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that national unity, progress and prosperity could only be achieved when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir said although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come. “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” he said. Sanusi also apologised for the delay in visiting Ladoja following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. The Emir described the courtesy visit as necessary, given the longstanding relationship between the two traditional institutions and their respective communities. Reflecting on his relationship with Ibadan, Sanusi recalled his longstanding connections with the ancient city dating back to his days at First Bank, his association with the late Aare Musulumi of Yorubaland, Alhaji Abdulazeez Arisekola Alao, and his subsequent tenure as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria. He said Ibadan had remained a familiar destination over the years, adding that he had maintained close relationships with several indigenes of the city. Sanusi also expressed his readiness to host the Olubadan in Kano, saying reciprocal visits would further strengthen the longstanding bonds between the two communities and promote understanding among Nigerians from different regions. Responding, Ladoja identified political interference in traditional institutions as a major concern, calling for deliberate measures to insulate traditional rulers from partisan politics and arbitrary decisions capable of destabilising established traditional structures. He warned that political actors who interfere in traditional institutions often take decisions without fully appreciating their historical significance and the far-reaching consequences for affected communities. Specifically, the Olubadan expressed concern over developments surrounding the Kano Emirate, arguing that an institution with more than 1,000 years of history should not be subjected to arbitrary fragmentation. He urged those involved in the controversy to allow reason to prevail, expressing hope that peace and the historical integrity of the Kano Emirate would be restored. “We have a lot in common. And we have to find a way of insulating the position of the traditional rulers from partisan politics, failure of which they continue to take decisions whose consequences they don’t even understand. “From history, we know that Kano has been there for more than 1,000 years. And for somebody to wake up and say he is going to break it doesn’t seem to be reasonable. We pray that reason will prevail in the Kano Emirate to restore what we used to know Kano for,” Ladoja said. Recalling the Maitatsine crisis, which originated in Kano, the Olubadan stressed the need to sustain peace in the ancient city, describing it as a major commercial centre whose stability has implications for the wider northern region and Nigeria. He noted that Kano and Ibadan were widely regarded as two of the country’s most accommodating cities, adding that Kano remained a major convergence point for Hausa- and Fulani-speaking communities. According to him, Kano’s importance as a commercial hub extended beyond Nigeria, making peace and stability in the city a matter of national importance. Ladoja also commended Sanusi for relinquishing his position as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria to ascend the throne of his ancestors, describing the decision as a reflection of his character, convictions and commitment to traditional service. He noted that the CBN governor occupied a strategic position in the management of Nigeria’s economy, adding that Sanusi’s decision to leave the office for the Kano throne demonstrated the importance he attached to his traditional heritage. The Olubadan further recalled admiring the Emir’s spiritual devotion during their encounters in Medina while performing Umrah, saying Sanusi remained committed to prayer even when he occupied the country’s foremost banking position. “Whoever is heading the Central Bank is virtually heading Nigeria’s economy, so to have left that office to become the Emir of Kano shows who you are. I used to admire him any time I went to Umrah; even as the Central Bank Governor, he was always on the same spot in Medina for hours praying,” he said. Ladoja, who disclosed that he was still in the first year of his reign, also explained the distinctive traditional succession system in Ibadanland, which operates a republican arrangement without a clearly defined ruling house. He said the emergence of an Olubadan followed a lengthy progression through the traditional chieftaincy hierarchy, requiring aspirants to climb 22 or 23 successive stages before attaining the throne. The monarch disclosed that his journey towards becoming Olubadan began in 1993 and lasted 32 years, expressing gratitude to Almighty Allah for making his ascension to the revered stool possible. “Ibadan, as you know it, is republican. There is no defined ruling house, and it is only the Almighty Allah that crowns the Olubadan of Ibadanland because you have to climb 22 or 23 ladders before you become the Olubadan. “I started my journey in 1993; that is a journey of 32 years. For that, I thank God that I am the Olubadan today,” he said. The Olubadan also pledged to reciprocate Sanusi’s visit by travelling to Kano, while recalling his longstanding friendship with a Kano elder, Yusuf Garba Ali, dating back to 1972. items.title: NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers
items.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has pledged a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state. Ajia made the pledge on Sunday in Ilorin while unveiling the NDC’s 2027 Gubernatorial Campaign Council manifesto, tagged ‘Forward Kwara Agenda’. He proposed a N120,000 public-service minimum wage benchmark and a cost-of-living adjustment framework for workers and pensioners. He said his administration would verify the payroll, assess the financial implications, consult labour unions and publish an implementation and funding timetable. On pensioners, Ajia promised to verify outstanding gratuities and publish a schedule for settling validated arrears. He also pledged to establish a predictable payment timetable for newly due pension obligations. Ajia said he entered the governorship race to make public institutions work reliably for all Kwarans, regardless of political affiliation. “I am running to make public institutions work that way. If entrusted with office, I will serve people who support me, people who oppose me and people who have never attended a political meeting,” he said. He said his experience as a teacher, researcher and university administrator had taught him to ask critical questions, examine evidence and take responsibility for results. Ajia, who led a School of Business and mentored young people, said his visits home exposed him to the challenges facing unemployed graduates. He said many young people could hardly predict when fair employment opportunities would become available. According to him, government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens understand how to access assistance, eligibility requirements and appeal procedures. He said access to public services should not depend on personal relationships with the governor. Ajia said the Forward Kwara Agenda outlined six areas of governance, anchored on stronger institutions, greater opportunities and shared prosperity. On security, he said farmers should access their farms, children should travel safely to school and traders should return home safely from markets. NAN reports that the event attracted hundreds of NDC stakeholders from the state’s 16 local government areas. The post NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach
items.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp praised Xavi Hernandez on Sunday, saying the new Netherlands coach already had the Dutch playing in his own image after just five games in charge. Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s meeting between the two old rivals, Klopp pointed to Friday’s 7-0 thumping of Greece in Amsterdam and said the former midfielder had made an impression. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. He also won the World Cup with Spain. “They simply played some electric football,” Klopp said, adding: “Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football… “He’s a coach who really pushes his approach to the limit. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. It will be a really good test for us,” Xavi said. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. They are the most important. I don’t need to convince them to play this style of football, they have the capacity to play like the last game. Germany and the Netherlands played out a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in September, the first match in charge for both Klopp and Xavi. Xavi said he would try and do the unexpected on Monday, but acknowledged it would not be easy against the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach. “It’s difficult to surprise a coach like Jurgen Klopp,” Xavi said. “He’s one of the best coaches in the past few years. And it’s an honour to come up against him tomorrow.” Vanguard News The post ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: APC mocks NDC over campaign spending claims
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress (APC) has mocked the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) over its criticism of the Federal Government’s spending priorities, accusing the opposition party of focusing on the ruling party’s campaign activities instead of preparing for the 2027 general election. The APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, described the NDC’s claims as “comical”, saying the party had appointed itself “Nigeria’s auditor-general of campaign financing” despite what he described as its limited electoral presence. Morka was reacting to a statement by the NDC National Campaign Council spokesperson, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, who accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of prioritising political publicity and patronage over critical sectors of the economy. Ikokwu had alleged that substantial resources were being spent on political publicity and the distribution of vehicles, laptops, sewing machines and food items by groups supporting Tinubu, while essential public services remained underfunded. She also questioned the government’s spending priorities in view of additional revenue accruing from the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes in taxation. On security and healthcare funding, the NDC spokesperson claimed that only about seven per cent of the Defence Capital Budget was released in 2025. She further alleged that only N36 million out of the N218 billion allocated to health capital expenditure was released in the same year, citing a reported disclosure by the Minister of Health. The opposition party also accused some APC-controlled state governments of similar spending practices, warning that political publicity and patronage could not conceal the consequences of poor governance. But dismissing the criticism, Morka said the NDC lacked the electoral footprint and political relevance to question the APC’s campaign activities. “It is rather comical that the NDC, a party that has no electoral footprint and is still struggling to establish its political identity and relevance, has suddenly appointed itself Nigeria’s auditor-general of campaign financing,” he said. Morka argued that the opposition party had become preoccupied with the APC’s campaign activities instead of developing its own platform and preparing for the forthcoming election. “The NDC has yet to initiate or show any capacity to conduct nationwide campaign activities as expected of any serious party. Instead, the party has continued to display its obsession about APC and its legitimate campaign activities,” he said. He added that the NDC was distracted by what he described as the APC’s coordinated campaign activities across the country. “The NDC is only jittery and dazed by the APC’s focused and well-coordinated campaign activities across the country rather than expend its energy crafting its own campaign platform ahead of the 2027 general election,” Morka said. items.title: NDDC allegation: Akpabio challenges Amaechi to produce evidence
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has challenged former Rivers State Governor and African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, to provide documentary evidence to substantiate his allegation that Akpabio introduced a 50 per cent deduction from payments to contractors of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC). Akpabio said public accountability required evidence rather than campaign declarations, insisting that allegations of wrongdoing must be supported by verifiable facts and subjected to appropriate investigation. He also said Amaechi’s eight-year tenure as governor of Rivers State deserved public scrutiny, particularly regarding expenditure and outcomes of major projects initiated by his administration. The Senate President’s position was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Hon. Eseme Eyiboh, in response to remarks attributed to Amaechi at an ADC political rally in Bauchi on Saturday, November 14, 2026. According to the statement, Amaechi had alleged that Akpabio introduced a 50 per cent deduction from payments due to NDDC contractors. Akpabio described the allegation as serious but said Amaechi had not provided contract documents, payment records, identifiable transactions or other verifiable details to support it. He challenged the former governor to identify the contracts involved, the affected contractors, when the alleged deductions occurred and the payment arrangements through which they were allegedly made. He also asked Amaechi to provide evidence establishing Akpabio’s personal involvement in the alleged deductions. The statement quoted Akpabio as saying: “Mr Amaechi is entitled to raise concerns about public administration. He is equally obliged to distinguish what he can substantiate from what he merely alleges. “The same standard applies to every public officeholder. We therefore invite him to place any credible documentary evidence in his possession before the appropriate authorities so that the issues he has raised may be examined objectively and in accordance with the law.” He added that public accountability was strengthened when allegations were tested against evidence, public expenditure examined against outcomes and institutions allowed to discharge their responsibilities without political interference. Amaechi’s Rivers record deserves scrutiny — Akpabio The Senate President said Amaechi’s tenure as Rivers State governor between 2007 and 2015 was also a legitimate subject of public examination, particularly concerning the cost, completion and sustainability of projects undertaken during the period. He specifically cited the Port Harcourt monorail project and the Malaria-Free Rivers State initiatives as examples of projects whose implementation and outcomes, according to him, raised questions about public expenditure and value for money. On the monorail project, Akpabio said its reported cost, incomplete implementation and inability to deliver the anticipated public transportation service warranted examination. He raised questions about the amount spent on the project, the extent to which its original objectives were achieved and the institutional and contractual decisions that contributed to its difficulties. According to him, public accountability should extend to every public official entrusted with public resources and authority, irrespective of political affiliation. “The credibility of a public allegation must rest not on the volume of its delivery, the status of its author or the occasion on which it is made, but on the quality of the evidence supporting it. Let the facts speak,” he said. 2027 elections Akpabio acknowledged that political disagreements would intensify as the country approaches the 2027 general elections, describing such disagreements as normal in a democracy. He, however, cautioned political actors against making unsubstantiated allegations capable of undermining public confidence in institutions. He said allegations concerning the NDDC’s contracts, finances and administration should be addressed through credible investigative processes rather than turned into instruments of political confrontation. The Senate President stressed that the people of the Niger Delta deserved functional infrastructure, transparent procurement, completed projects and measurable development outcomes. He added that the interests of the region should remain central to discussions about the commission and its responsibilities. items.title: 2027: NDC accuses Tinubu of prioritising campaign propaganda over budgets
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of prioritising campaign propaganda and political patronage over funding critical sectors of the economy, alleging that the huge spending on political publicity explains the poor implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets. The opposition party challenged the Federal Government to publish verifiable figures showing how much had been released for critical capital projects and administrative subventions in the three fiscal years, compared with expenditure on political advertisements and patronage. The NDC made the allegations in a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of its National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, titled, “Dear Mr. President: The Huge Cost of Your Campaign Propaganda Testifies to Why You Failed to Adequately Fund 2024, 2025 and 2026 Budgets.” The party said its assessment of what it described as a barrage of political advertisements, donations, vehicles, laptops, sewing machines, food items and other gifts distributed by groups and individuals claiming to support Tinubu had raised questions about the administration’s spending priorities. It alleged that despite increased government revenue following the removal of fuel subsidy and higher taxation, critical social and physical infrastructure, national security and citizens’ welfare had not received adequate funding. Ikokwu said: “For instance, despite the palpable insecurity confronting the nation, only about seven per cent of the Defence Capital Budget was reportedly released in 2025. “Even more disturbing was when the Minister of Health reported that only ₦36 million out of the ₦218 billion allocated to Health Capital expenditure was released in the same 2025.” The party argued that the alleged low releases for defence and health raised questions about the government’s commitment to addressing insecurity and improving public services. It also expressed concern over the implementation of the 2026 budget, which it claimed had received inadequate attention, and accused the APC of devoting substantial resources to campaign publicity and political patronage ahead of the 2027 elections. Questioning the administration’s spending priorities, Ikokwu asked how a government benefiting from fuel subsidy removal and increased taxation could plead a lack of funds for national security, healthcare, education, federal roads and the welfare of ordinary Nigerians while political activities appeared to attract substantial resources. The NDC also alleged that several state governments, particularly those it claimed had been pressured into joining the APC, had poor records of budget implementation but had sufficient resources for campaign propaganda. The party further linked what it described as poor governance and deteriorating infrastructure to the rising incidents of political intimidation and violence, alleging that such developments could be aimed at discouraging voters from participating in the January 2027 elections. It, however, warned that propaganda, political patronage and intimidation could not permanently conceal the consequences of poor governance. “The NDC therefore challenges the Tinubu administration to explain its budgetary priorities and demonstrate, with verifiable figures, how much has actually been released for critical capital projects and administrative subventions in 2024, 2025 and 2026, as against the resources expended on political publicity and patronage by sundry characters,” the statement said. The party also declared that its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, would prioritise accountability, public service funding and a transition from a consumption-driven to a production-based economy if elected in 2027. “The Obi/Kwankwaso administration will be accountable; will fund public services and move the country from consumption to production,” it added. items.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 ends in vibrant celebration of Ghanaian enterprise after three days of business, shopping and entertainment
items.description: The 2026 Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair has successfully concluded after three exciting days of business exhibitions, product displays, shopping bargains, networking, cultural performances and live music, transforming Ghud Park at Accra Mall into a vibrant marketplace for Ghanaian entrepreneurs and consumers. The three-day event, which ran from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, brought together more than 80 businesses and brands across various sectors, giving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) an opportunity to showcase their products, attract customers, generate sales and establish valuable business connections. From locally processed foods, spices and refreshing beverages to fashionable clothing, beauty products, electronics, agricultural produce, household essentials and innovative technology solutions, the fair offered patrons an extensive range of products and services to explore and purchase. Organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank and powered by JoyPrime, the exhibition combined business promotion with entertainment, creating an engaging experience for exhibitors, shoppers, families and other visitors. Three days of business, music and unforgettable experiences The opening day on Friday, November 13, set the pace for the exhibition, with participating businesses welcoming patrons and displaying products across different categories. Ghud Park quickly became a bustling shopping destination, with colourful exhibition stands, product demonstrations and vendors engaging visitors eager to discover new brands and take advantage of attractive offers. Joy Prime’s KMJ and popular content creator Quecy Official added excitement to the opening-day activities, interacting with exhibitors and patrons and bringing additional visibility to the businesses participating in the fair. Nkyimkyim Band also featured among the musical acts, adding to the live entertainment and giving patrons more reasons to remain at the exhibition and enjoy the atmosphere. Patrons sang along, danced and captured memorable moments, while vendors who had spent hours promoting their products also joined the celebrations. The atmosphere was characterised by the aroma of freshly prepared meals, colourful fashion displays, beauty products, electronic gadgets and household essentials, as shoppers moved from one stand to another exploring the offerings. Saturday, November 14, brought another dimension to the event as Ghanaian music duo Lali X Lola and King Jerry delivered energetic performances that transformed the exhibition grounds into a lively celebration. Patrons sang along, danced and captured the moments on their phones, while vendors who had spent hours promoting their products also joined the entertainment. In some memorable scenes, exhibitors carried their merchandise onto the dance floor as they danced, creating an unusual but exciting blend of business promotion and musical entertainment. The second-day performances demonstrated the fair’s ability to attract visitors beyond conventional shopping activities, allowing businesses to connect with customers in a relaxed and entertaining environment. The excitement continued on Sunday, November 15, with the Kekeli Borborbor Group bringing the traditional rhythms and energetic dance traditions of the Volta Region to the exhibition. The cultural performance was complemented by a live-band appearance from Shakers Band, giving patrons another opportunity to enjoy music and dancing while exploring the various exhibition stands. The Borborbor display brought a distinctive cultural touch to the final-day activities, while Shakers Band maintained the entertainment atmosphere, providing a fitting conclusion to three days of business, culture and celebration. Food lovers treated to an impressive variety One of the biggest attractions throughout the fair was the wide selection of food products, beverages and agricultural produce presented by participating businesses. Wilmar Africa showcased its Fortune Spread brand, while Kivo, Didi Shito, Corki Ventures, Adjoor Ventures, Manellah Foods, Gold Coast Foods with its Sankofa Spices, and Yaapee Royal Foods were among the businesses displaying food products and locally processed goods. Other food exhibitors included NutriSmart Ventures, Golden Parani Company Limited, G-Way Investments Africa Limited, Ikam Plus Company Limited and ESBONY Food Package, which specialises in repackaging finished goods. For beverage enthusiasts, Koa Impact Commerce showcased natural cocoa juice, Delsoy Ltd presented soy milk, Orave Juices offered fruit juice, while Pinnacle Coco Limited displayed coconut juice. Jussvina Drinks (Global 500), Green Cup, which featured beetroot, guava and pawpaw teas, and Myst Natural Water also added to the beverage selection. BB Brothers and Mushroom General were among other exhibitors, with the latter showcasing processed mushroom products. Agricultural businesses, including Farm Mate, Orrab Farms, T&C Farms and Atohfield, presented agricultural and fresh-produce offerings. Those looking for freshly prepared meals were also catered for, with Flourish Foods Africa showcasing grilled chicken and poultry products, MamsiJoy Ventures offering rice, Ellie Catering Services presenting fufu, Martha’s Yam Trading specialising in yam, and Selis Satisfactory displaying kenkey. The food section was further enriched by Di Dwa Foods, Bliss Pop, 97 Bakes, Aladdin Bakery, Evive Delight Ltd and Desco Ltd, which showcased snacks, baked products, popcorn and processed foods. Fashion, beauty and lifestyle take centre stage Fashion enthusiasts had plenty to explore, with Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Asangenta, Utonez Clothier, Kofikyere Klothing, Regy Couture Ltd, Kims Foods and Clothings, and JAT Couture showcasing clothing, dresses, bags and accessories. Shoes Ts3 presented footwear for different sizes, while Kinky Love Crochet displayed hair products and wigs. Beauty and personal-care brands were also well represented, with Haus of Lush, RNS Beauty, Leepoku Ventures, Atlas Prime Merchantile Ltd and Chocho showcasing their products. Mist and Strands presented bath and body products, while Reed Diffusers Ghana Ltd and Esquicet Scents exhibited home-fragrance products, including diffusers and scented candles. Liz Imports showcased perfumes and home appliances, Kemz Ceramics displayed ceramic products, and Eldem Floral Services presented fresh-cut flowers. Businesses catering for mothers, children and families also participated, including Roses Enterprise, Mothercare and Prestige Children’s Palace. The variety gave shoppers opportunities to explore fashion, beauty and lifestyle products while interacting directly with the businesses behind the brands. Technology, electronics and household solutions The exhibition also provided a platform for technology companies and businesses offering practical solutions for homes, offices and commercial activities. Galop Sea Limited showcased laptops and accessories, while Xfromo Hypermart displayed mobile phones and accessories, including Google Pixel devices. Katon 360 Technologies presented a digital platform designed to support SMEs, while Solid Connect showcased an application for artisans. We Shop Africa and Ayuda represented the e-commerce sector, offering visitors opportunities to explore digital shopping solutions. Atlantic Meridian EV showcased electric vehicles, while Vital Vendors presented car essentials. For household and construction needs, Sintex Tank exhibited water-storage solutions, DBS showcased housing and roofing products, and MGIG Suppliers presented powdered soap. Worafam Group of Companies displayed safety wear, while Greenhaul Solutions showcased waste-management and scrap-procurement services. Other participating businesses included Vaal Real Estate, Advantage GH Premium Apparel, Blessed 3 Ventures, Gorgeous Vie Event Hub, Grandeur Consult Travel and Tour, Astolinks and Afram Publication. BB Chemist also participated with its Relax Liver Salt product, while Golden Pride (Yao Consult) represented the liquor retail sector. Major institutions strengthen participation Established institutions and major brands also featured prominently, adding to the diversity of the exhibition. Ecobank, MTN, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), Glico Life and Central University were among the participating institutions. Their presence provided opportunities for visitors to explore banking, telecommunications, insurance, export promotion and educational services, complementing the wide range of products and services offered by smaller businesses. The participation of established institutions alongside emerging enterprises demonstrated the fair’s ability to bring different players in Ghana’s business ecosystem together. A significant platform for Ghanaian SMEs Beyond the entertainment and shopping experience, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair provided participating businesses with an opportunity to increase brand visibility, introduce new products, engage potential customers, generate sales and establish commercial relationships. For many exhibitors, the direct interaction with consumers offered an opportunity to explain their products, receive feedback and demonstrate the value of their offerings. Patrons, on the other hand, benefited from having access to a wide range of products in one location, with opportunities to compare offerings, explore promotional deals and purchase directly from business owners. The 2026 edition builds on the maiden fair held in October 2025, which attracted more than 160 exhibitors and recorded over 1,000 visitors on its opening day. The latest exhibition’s participation by more than 80 businesses and brands across food and beverages, fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, finance, real estate and lifestyle sectors further highlighted the diversity of Ghanaian enterprise. The event also demonstrated how entertainment can complement business exhibitions by attracting audiences, keeping patrons engaged and creating memorable experiences around participating brands. A vibrant celebration of enterprise As the curtains came down on the 2026 edition, the three-day exhibition had offered a compelling combination of commerce, culture and entertainment. From KMJ and Quecy Official’s opening-day engagements to the musical performances of Lali X Lola and King Jerry, and the traditional Borborbor rhythms of the Kekeli Borborbor Group alongside Shakers Band’s live performance, each day brought a distinct attraction to the fair. The enthusiastic participation of vendors, the diversity of products on display and the entertainment programme helped make the exhibition a memorable meeting point for businesses and consumers. For the participating SMEs, it was an opportunity to take their brands directly to the marketplace, reach potential customers and explore new commercial opportunities. For patrons, it was three days of shopping, discovery, entertainment and support for Ghanaian businesses. It was a vibrant celebration of Ghanaian creativity, innovation, entrepreneurship and the growing potential of small and medium-sized businesses.

items.title: Lagos APC faults Obi, NDC over singing old national anthem
items.description: …Questions opposition’s focus on national development By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, has criticised former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and members of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, over their singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem at a recent town hall meeting. The party’s spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who reacted to the development, described the action as political theatrics and nostalgia rather than a focus on national development. Oladejo argued that national symbols should not be used selectively for partisan purposes, noting that Nigeria adopted its current national anthem through a lawful process. He said the incident reflected what he described as a pattern in which Obi’s public conduct appeared influenced by the immediate sentiments of his political audience. According to him, aspiring to lead a country of more than 200 million people requires independent judgment, intellectual discipline and respect for established national institutions. “A president must possess the temperament to listen to his supporters without becoming captive to their sentiments,” Oladejo said, adding that leadership required providing direction even when it differed from the immediate expectations of supporters. The APC spokesman also questioned the consistency of Obi’s political alignments and policy agenda, citing reports that the former Anambra governor had described his current presidential ambition as a “valedictory shot” at the presidency. He maintained that the office of the president required a clear and implementable development programme rather than symbolic gestures. Addressing the NDC, Oladejo said political parties were expected to present credible policy alternatives and provide clear direction on governance rather than operate as what he described as “cultural nostalgia clubs.” He argued that singing the former national anthem would not address pressing national challenges, including unemployment, insecurity, infrastructure deficits and economic hardship. The Lagos APC urged Nigerians to scrutinise the policy positions, consistency and respect for national institutions demonstrated by those seeking political leadership, while reaffirming its commitment to what it described as forward-looking governance. items.title: Kédougou : 65 millions de FCFA investis dans la réalisation d’une gare routière
items.description: La commune de Kédougou a inauguré ce dimanche sa nouvelle gare routière, aménagée sur un site de quatre hectares pour un coût de 65 millions de FCFA. Cette réalisation met fin à plus de 25 ans d’attente pour les transporteurs et les populations. Selon Ibrahima Diouf, directeur financier et administratif de la mairie, le projet est le fruit d’un travail engagé depuis 2022 par l’équipe municipale du maire Ousmane Sylla, en collaboration avec les transporteurs et les services techniques. Les travaux ont notamment permis le remblayage du site, la construction de six bureaux, l’aménagement de hangars et de blocs sanitaires, ainsi que l’installation de points d’eau potable. La gare dispose également de 23 lampadaires solaires et d’équipements électriques pour renforcer la sécurité et l’éclairage. La gestion quotidienne de l’infrastructure est confiée au bureau des transporteurs, avec l’accompagnement de la mairie. La salubrité sera assurée grâce à des opérations régulières de nettoyage avec l’appui de l’UCG. Les occupants sont également invités à participer à l’entretien du site. Si la gare est désormais fonctionnelle, certains travaux d’aménagement se poursuivent. Pour la municipalité, l’objectif est de garantir aux voyageurs et aux professionnels du transport un cadre plus sûr, organisé et salubre. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: NDC Regional Elections: Walewale supporters allege sabotage after former parliamentary candidate wins Regional Secretary
items.description: Supporters of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Walewale have accused officials of the North East Regional Coordinating Directorate of deliberately frustrating celebrations following the election of former Walewale parliamentary candidate, Abubakari Abdallah, as the party’s Regional Secretary. The supporters allege that electricity supply to Walewale was deliberately disconnected shortly after the party’s regional executive elections on Saturday, November 14, 2026, to prevent them from celebrating Mr Abdallah’s victory. Power went off in the township a few minutes after the election results were declared, with Mr Abdallah and several other candidates emerging victorious. JoyNews checks confirmed that the outage affected Walewale, while electricity supply in other parts of the region remained uninterrupted. Power was subsequently restored to the township at about 11:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 15. The incident has triggered angry reactions among Mr Abdallah’s supporters, many of whom have taken to social media to condemn what they describe as an attempt to undermine the former parliamentary candidate. Some have accused officials of the Northern Electricity Distribution Company (NEDCo) of allowing the electricity distribution network to be drawn into what they consider a political vendetta against Mr Abdallah, who has contested the Walewale parliamentary seat three times. One supporter directly accused the North East Regional Minister, Ibrahim Tia, of being behind the alleged blackout, although no evidence was provided to substantiate the claim. However, there is no independent evidence to establish that the outage was politically motivated or that any government official or NEDCo personnel deliberately disconnected electricity to frustrate the celebrations. Several attempts by JoyNews to reach NEDCo officials in Walewale for comments were unsuccessful. Rauf Tanko retains regional chairmanship amid inducement allegations Meanwhile, incumbent NDC North East Regional Chairman, Abdul Rauf Tanko Ibrahim, has retained his position after securing 146 votes. His re-election has, however, attracted attention following his admission during an interview with journalists that he distributed motorbikes and other forms of support to delegates ahead of the elections. Responding to questions about allegations of vote-buying, Mr Tanko acknowledged distributing motorbikes but defended the gesture as part of his responsibilities as the incumbent regional chairman. “It is not only motorbikes that were given to delegates,” he told journalists. “Don’t forget that I am the incumbent Regional Chairman. Before winning this election, it was my duty to finance or fund the party’s activities in the region. So, I don’t think it is misplaced for me to buy motorbikes for executives to enable them to carry out party activities across the region,” he added. Full list of elected NDC North East Regional Executives The November 14 elections produced the following winners: Regional Chairman Abdul Rauf Tanko Ibrahim – 146 votes Regional Vice Chairman John Bibirim – 100 votes Regional Secretary Abdallah Abubakari – 114 votes Deputy Regional Secretary Thomas B. Jayen – 95 votes Regional Organiser Godfred Mayeem – 124 votes Deputy Regional Organiser Mohammed Akunloya – 97 votes Regional Treasurer Ibrahim Rasheed – 94 votes Deputy Regional Treasurer Nurudini Abdul-Rahaman – 136 votes Regional Communications Officer A. Abdul Gafaru Mohammed – 108 votes Deputy Regional Communications Officer Hamza Iddrisu Salifu – 70 votes Regional Women’s Organiser Sumaya Ligbi Salifu Deputy Regional Women’s Organiser Asana Yidana Regional Youth Organiser Fatawu Karandey Amidu Deputy Regional Youth Organisers Kamil Dabri Ibrahim Yussif Sulemana Saeed Zongo Caucus Coordinator Tahiru Rafiu – 80 votes A total of 231 delegates participated in the regional elections held at the Nalerigu Senior High School. More than 200 police officers were deployed to the election grounds to maintain security. The officers arrived unarmed, with the police commander explaining that the arrangement was intended to ensure a peaceful and impartial electoral process. He said armed personnel remained on standby to respond to any eventuality. The elections form part of the NDC’s internal reorganisation ahead of the party’s national executive elections scheduled for December 19, 2026. Abuba’s victory comes against the backdrop of tensions with Regional Minister Mr Abdallah’s election as Regional Secretary comes against the backdrop of a prolonged political disagreement between his supporters and North East Regional Minister Ibrahim Tia, largely centred on influence within the NDC and access to government appointments. The tensions became increasingly public in November 2025 when supporters of Mr Abdallah accused the Regional Minister, the Regional Chairman and other party executives of deliberately frustrating the former parliamentary candidate’s attempts to secure a government appointment. The aggrieved supporters also complained that several grassroots activists who worked for the party during the 2024 general elections had been overlooked in government appointments, while individuals they considered less active in the party had been rewarded with influential positions. Some further accused regional party executives of circulating damaging reports about Mr Abdallah and his associates, including allegations that some of them engaged in skirt-and-blouse voting during the 2024 elections. Mr Tia rejected the allegations, insisting that neither he nor the regional executives had deliberately worked against the former parliamentary candidate. In an interview with JoyNews on November 19, 2025, the Regional Minister argued that contesting parliamentary elections or supporting the NDC did not automatically entitle anyone to a government appointment. “He is not the only one who contested and hasn’t been appointed,” Mr Tia said, citing other former parliamentary candidates in the region who had also not received government positions. He also denied claims that regional executives had submitted reports to discredit Mr Abdallah, explaining that the party obtained information about constituency activities through several channels, including national-level party officials. The disagreement subsequently spilled into the party’s grassroots structures in Walewale, with aggrieved supporters threatening to boycott party activities over what they described as the marginalisation of loyal members. On December 7, 2025, regional executives, including Mr Tia and Regional Chairman Rauf Tanko, held an emergency meeting with aggrieved party members in Walewale. The meeting followed weeks of agitation over government appointments and allegations that influential regional figures were sidelining Mr Abdallah and his supporters. A joint committee comprising regional executives and constituency representatives was established to examine the complaints and recommend measures to address the divisions. Mr Abdallah’s victory in the November 14, 2026 elections is therefore politically significant, particularly against the backdrop of competing interests within the party in the constituency.

items.title: The stench of cocaine and Ghana’s new cedi – Occasional Kwatriot Kwesi Yankah writes
items.description: On my global rounds last year, I was shocked to see at airport shops perfume names that shook me to the core: a perfume called ‘Cocaine,’ then another designer perfume. ‘Opium.’ But the killer of them all was ‘Sinners Perfume,’ apparently the fastest ticket to Hell. Surprisingly, the accompanying aromas were smooth, except that no Daddy in his right senses would want ‘Cocaine Perfume’ even mistakenly seized by Customs officials. Those were on sale for $175 to $200, and attracted a small queue of young men. The trip to the cocaine world is not as long as you thought. Who knows if we have a cocaine heritage on our hands in Ghana, in search of heritage items on a new currency. Our beloved country has now launched new currency bank notes, called the ‘heritage series’: a label we are scratching our heads to understand. Are the current cedi notes that weak and fragile, their batteries about to die? Or does the Bank of Ghana seek an excuse to print new money and fill the till to rescue 2028? ‘There is no money in the system,’ market women complain of low sales; so ‘let’s simply print more money and give it an elegant pseudonym, Heritage? Were the signs not clear? Did you notice the speed, the rush, the sense of urgency, and eventually the anti-climax: a comedy of errors on our sovereign cedi. National mourning, indeed, tears for a sinking Ghana. For once, the entire public is part of this debate on our national heritage; and we are together debating wrong faces matched to human names on new currency notes; and we lament essentials missing in the national heritage. Indeed, faces on our new cedi notes have sparked so much debate that we forget the likelihood that Artificial Intelligence may have fooled us all. Let Ghana wait until rumours spread that the man we see as Kofi Annan on the new 100 cedi note is really not Kofi Annan but our friend Kevin Taylor; and that the lady displayed as Justice Annie Jiagge on the new 10 cedi note is ‘before God and man,’ probably Akosua Jollof? Simply imagine the stampede online. It is now unclear whether the Bank of Ghana will swallow its pride and go back to school for remedial education: honouring the name Theodocia Okoh with the true Face of Theodocia Okoh, the true designer of the national flag. Letitia Obeng, the mistaken identity, was well known to us fellows of the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences. She was an award-winning scientist who, in 2006, succeeded Nana Dr S.K.B. Asante as the first female President of the Academy. ‘Auntie Leti’ must be stirring in her grave over her mixed identity with Theodosia. Then comes, of late, a damning verdict on the picture representation of Cardinal Peter Dery on the two cedi note. Says a worried Ghanaian: “It is simply disheartening and baffling that a national tribute meant to honour an iconic figure of our faith, the late Cardinal Peter Dery of blessed memory, could be marred by such a glaring oversight.” Cardinal Peter Dery Cardinal Peter Dery Then was this blatant omission of five of the Big Six on the heritage bank notes, leaving a lone Kwame Nkrumah. Remember the Big Six statue in Accra was demolished in 2024 by an anonymous Ghanaian at dawn, who had enough time to videotape the entire event in full view of cheering spectators. It was during the Nana Addo era. No arrests were made by the police, who were three hundred meters away. When the Mahama party won power in late 2024, the Big Six roundabout was redesigned, with the Big Six statue conspicuously deleted. The Big Six, with Nkrumah, Danquah, Edward Akufo Addo, Obetsebi Lamptey, Ako Adjei, and William Ofori Atta, is apparently no longer a heritage priority? But wait till power changes hands in 2028; Ghana’s toy play may bounce back. And what do we do with this bizarre incident? 2021 one Esther Bosha a Zimbabwean national and crew member of Emirate Air, visits Ghana as tourist, poses for a picture among market women in Accra; then says a word or two in praise of Ghana. A kind-hearted Bank of Ghana adds her picture among traders, as qualified to stick on Ghana’s one cedi banknote. Esther Bosha as Ghana’s heritage icon? Zimbabwe currently chuckles hearing this. I myself visited Zimbabwe in 2006 and felt at home seeing Mugabe’s Zanu-PF headquarters in Harare, hoisting the Red Cockerel flag of Kwame Nkrumah’s CPP. I warmly applauded, but did that qualify me to appear on the Zimbabwean currency? Where is our state protocol? Our parliament? Ghana, when did we drop the baton and lose the plot? And how did we sink this low? Our state emblems now run the ship of state aground, and all is quiet? Akom ko, the elders say. ‘The pristine dance of the high priest is no more, leaving the field for those that merely twirl around in raffia skirts… Ghana is no longer the state we knew: now plunged into a crisis of identity, prewired with a badge of dishonour. We miserably flopped at the soccer World Cup, but beat our chest with pride, excelling in a global cocaine league. Daily news breaks of Drugs shipped through our ports, sometimes officially escorted. Our port officials see no cocaine, speak no cocaine, smell no cocaine and do no cocaine. But kids do cocaine at home and school. The scandal breaks only after the horse has left the stable…When cocaine arrests are made, no names and no faces. Indeed, a silent cocaine prosecution in a nation that is not angry enough to crack the whip. Yes, we have a heritage to protect, and display on bank notes, but it is Negative Heritage. A sordid heritage of moving sewage that was once called rivers; a heritage of toxic streams, poisoned crops, dangerous turbidity. No river has been spared, including the great Volta River, and with it the diverse fish species it hosts. The school kids are busy too, learning the sport of poisoning; they have abandoned school and now mine in poisonous waters. After all this, we finally set our sights on the sea, to seal the shipment of floating sewage. But we shouldn’t omit paedophilia from the emerging heritage. Our moral compass is gone; elders and security now look on while school kids are defiled. Is anybody home, Ghana? A new cedi note has been launched in the filth of a negative heritage. That is the legacy we leave for future generations: the stench of cocaine across the landscape, in schools, a nation high on drugs, and a polluted banknote that says it all: A rotten heritage can only be returned to the Sender. How much has Ghana lost in all this? There is something they call Financial loss to the state. Hello Attorney General! Next Post: Yours truly as a Drug Suspect at Heathrow. kyankah@ashesi.edu.gh

items.title: Ghanaian community leaders in Toronto urged to step up as gun violence claims young lives
items.description: The growing number of young people losing their lives to gun violence in parts of Canada has prompted renewed calls for Ghanaian parents and community leaders to take a more active role in protecting the next generation. The appeal, directed at parents, traditional authorities and community associations in Toronto, comes amid grief over the reported killings of young people, including Javits Frimpong in New York, 18-year-old Malik Abass in Toronto and, most recently, Brandon Blake in Etobicoke. For Kwei Armah, a member of the Ghanaian community, the deaths should serve as a wake-up call to families and leaders who may not be paying enough attention to the challenges confronting young people growing up abroad. In an emotional appeal, he urged parents to look beyond providing their children with material needs and become more involved in their everyday lives. “Dear parents and leaders of our Ghanaian community, please wake up and take your children’s and siblings’ security seriously as the devil is at work!” he said. He believes parents must make time to understand their children’s experiences, friendships, difficulties and concerns, rather than assume that providing food, clothing and education is enough to secure their future. “Please engage your children in more conversations as to how you can raise them well, train them well and educate them well by paying more attention to their needs than attending funerals, parties and barbecues,” he appealed. His comments reflect growing concern about the vulnerability of some young people in immigrant communities, where parents may be balancing demanding work schedules, family responsibilities and the challenges of raising children in a different social environment. For many Ghanaian families who moved to Canada in search of better opportunities, securing a brighter future for their children remains a central part of the migration dream. But the recent deaths have brought a painful reminder that access to education, employment and other opportunities cannot guarantee a future if young people are exposed to violence and other dangers. Another young life lost The latest concern follows the fatal shooting of 18-year-old Brandon Blake of Barrie near Martin Grove Road and Finch Avenue West in Toronto. According to a Toronto Police Service news release published on Wednesday, November 11, officers responded to reports of gunshots at about 12:56 a.m. on Tuesday, November 10. Officers found Blake suffering from gunshot wounds. Despite life-saving efforts, he was pronounced dead at the scene. Police said two suspects fled before officers arrived. Investigators have identified 19-year-old Joseph Kunene of Toronto as a suspect wanted for first-degree murder. Police have released his photograph and described him as armed and dangerous. A second suspect, described as a white male wearing black clothing, a hood and a face mask, remains unidentified. The killing was recorded as Toronto’s 34th homicide of 2026, according to the police release. The deaths of Blake and Abass, alongside the reported killing of Frimpong in New York, have intensified concerns among sections of the Ghanaian community about the safety of young people. Although the circumstances surrounding the separate incidents remain subject to police investigations, the tragedies have prompted questions about how families and community institutions can better support young people and help prevent violence. A call for stronger community involvement Mr Armah believes the responsibility for protecting young people should not rest with parents alone. He is urging chiefs, religious leaders, community associations and other influential members of the Ghanaian diaspora to make youth welfare a consistent priority. He argues that community engagement should go beyond organising social gatherings and coming together to mourn after a tragedy. “Let our future leaders live. Brood over them, let them go to school and take advantage of the wonderful career opportunities that abound in this country,” he said. His appeal is for more deliberate conversations, mentorship and guidance to help young people navigate the pressures and risks they encounter. For Ghanaian community leaders, this could mean creating more opportunities for young people to speak openly about their experiences, connecting them with trusted mentors and strengthening support systems for families. The challenge is to ensure that youth safety becomes a shared responsibility rather than an issue that receives attention only when another life is lost. The Ghanaian community in Canada has worked over the years to preserve its cultural identity, support families and create opportunities for the next generation. Mr Armah’s message is that these efforts must also place greater emphasis on the safety, wellbeing and upbringing of young people. His appeal is simple: parents must be present in their children’s lives, community leaders must take a more active interest in their welfare, and families must act before another tragedy strikes.

items.title: Éducation : un mois après la rentrée, la COSYDEP alerte sur les fragilités persistantes de l’école sénégalaise
items.description: Un mois après la reprise effective des cours, le système éducatif sénégalais reste confronté à d’importantes difficultés structurelles. Dans une note d’analyse publiée en novembre 2026, la Coalition des organisations en synergie pour la défense de l’éducation publique (COSYDEP) relève notamment la persistance des inondations dans les établissements, la surcharge des classes, les déficits d’enseignants et les tensions sociales. L’organisation pointe surtout le décalage entre les engagements annoncés et leur traduction concrète dans les écoles. L’ouverture des classes ne signifie pas nécessairement que les conditions d’apprentissage sont réunies. C’est l’un des principaux enseignements de la note d’analyse de la COSYDEP consacrée à la situation de l’école sénégalaise un mois après la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027. À partir d’une enquête menée dans six régions (Dakar, Kaolack, Saint-Louis, Diourbel, Tambacounda et Sédhiou), complétée par une revue documentaire et l’examen des décisions gouvernementales, l’organisation dresse le tableau d’un système éducatif qui peine encore à résorber ses difficultés structurelles. Premier point de préoccupation : les conséquences des inondations. Malgré le report de cinq jours de la rentrée des élèves, initialement prévue le 7 octobre avant d’être effective le 12 octobre, plusieurs établissements continuaient de fonctionner dans des conditions sanitaires et pédagogiques difficiles. Sur les 53 écoles inondées suivies par l’enquête, 52 avaient repris leurs activités, tandis qu’une fonctionnait partiellement. Toutefois, 24 établissements, soit 45 % de l’échantillon, présentaient encore des risques liés notamment aux eaux stagnantes et à la remontée de la nappe phréatique. À l’école élémentaire Thiaroye Gare B, à Dakar, une seule des deux salles de cours de cours d’initiation (CI) était libérée des eaux. Les deux groupes d’élèves devaient ainsi partager l’espace disponible. À Kaolack, plusieurs établissements n’avaient toujours pas bénéficié de pulvérisation, faute de produits nécessaires auprès des services d’hygiène. Pour la COSYDEP, cette situation montre que la remise en service d’une école ne signifie pas nécessairement que celle-ci présente toutes les garanties sanitaires requises. Au-delà de l’urgence climatique, l’organisation attire l’attention sur les inégalités territoriales que cette situation entretient. Les élèves des zones les plus exposées cumulent souvent plusieurs handicaps : établissements inondés, difficultés de déplacement, insuffisance de mobilier et conditions d’apprentissage dégradées. Autre sujet de préoccupation, la surcharge des classes de sixième. Selon les données recueillies, l’effectif moyen est passé de 62 élèves par classe en 2024-2025 à 67 en 2025-2026, puis à 76 pour la présente année scolaire. Cette progression représente une hausse de 22,6 % en deux ans. La COSYDEP relève que cette situation exerce une pression supplémentaire sur les infrastructures, les équipements et les capacités d’encadrement des établissements. Les enseignants interrogés signalent également des difficultés de lecture et une baisse du niveau de certains élèves, particulièrement chez les garçons. Sans établir de lien de causalité automatique avec la suppression du concours d’entrée en sixième, l’organisation estime que l’élargissement de l’accès au collège doit être accompagné de mesures permettant d’absorber les nouveaux effectifs. Elle rappelle notamment le rôle du Certificat de fin d’études élémentaires (CFEE) dans la certification des acquis et la nécessité de veiller à la maîtrise des compétences fondamentales avant le passage au moyen. La réforme de l’orientation scientifique constitue un autre point de vigilance. Dans l’échantillon étudié, la proportion d’élèves orientés en seconde scientifique est passée de 15 % à près de 42 % entre 2025-2026 et 2026-2027. Les effectifs de cette série ont ainsi triplé, passant de 90 à 272 élèves, tandis que la moyenne par classe atteint désormais 68 élèves, contre 63 en seconde littéraire. Pour la COSYDEP, cette évolution quantitative doit impérativement s’accompagner d’un renforcement des capacités d’accueil. Les filières scientifiques nécessitent en effet des laboratoires fonctionnels, des professeurs spécialisés, des travaux pratiques et un encadrement pédagogique adapté. L’organisation recommande notamment de généraliser les cours de renforcement et de suivre attentivement le taux de passage de la seconde S en première S, considéré comme un indicateur important pour apprécier les effets de cette réforme. Les difficultés ne concernent pas uniquement les infrastructures et les effectifs. Le coût de la scolarité continue également de peser sur les ménages. D’après les moyennes établies par la COSYDEP dans les six régions étudiées, un élève du public, du CI à la seconde, représente une dépense moyenne de 23 767 FCFA en 2026-2027, contre 76 790 FCFA dans le privé. Sur deux ans, ces coûts ont progressé respectivement de 4,5 % et 8,3 %. La hausse est particulièrement marquée en seconde dans le privé, où les dépenses moyennes atteignent 99 400 FCFA, soit une progression de 15,5 % en deux ans. Dans le public, la sixième enregistre la plus forte augmentation, avec 9,5 %. Pour illustrer le poids de ces dépenses, la coalition estime qu’un ménage ayant trois enfants inscrits respectivement au CI, en sixième et en seconde doit mobiliser environ 74 500 FCFA dans le public et 235 850 FCFA dans le privé, hors transport et alimentation. Sur le plan des ressources humaines, les déficits demeurent importants dans plusieurs territoires. À Kaolack, l’enquête fait état d’un manque de 355 enseignants, dont 124 dans le préscolaire et l’élémentaire et 231 dans le moyen et le secondaire. La région enregistre également un déficit de plus de 9 000 tables-bancs. À Vélingara, les données font ressortir un besoin net de 59 enseignants et la persistance de 380 salles construites en huttes ou en lattes de bambou. À Tivaouane, le déficit en tables-bancs est estimé à 12 335 unités. Ces difficultés interviennent alors que l’État a annoncé le déploiement de plus de 8 400 enseignants, notamment à travers les sortants des structures de formation et le recrutement spécial de 2 527 enseignants. La COSYDEP demande ainsi la publication de leur répartition par académie, discipline et niveau, afin de mieux apprécier l’adéquation entre les besoins des établissements et les affectations réalisées. La question du temps scolaire et du dialogue social constitue également un enjeu majeur. Après une année 2025-2026 marquée par environ 150 heures de grève, le protocole d’accord signé le 16 avril 2026 entre le gouvernement et le G7 n’a pas empêché de nouvelles perturbations. Les syndicats ont observé une grève d’avertissement de 72 heures, du 21 au 23 octobre, dénonçant notamment des retards de paiement d’indemnités et de salaires ainsi que des difficultés liées à la formation diplômante. Pour la COSYDEP, ces tensions montrent que le pacte de stabilité sociale reste à consolider. L’organisation souligne notamment la nécessité de rendre pleinement opérationnel le comité de suivi des accords et de mettre à la disposition des différentes parties des éléments vérifiables sur l’état d’exécution des engagements. C’est d’ailleurs sur le terrain de la mise en œuvre des décisions publiques que la note formule l’une de ses principales observations. Le Conseil interministériel du 25 septembre 2026 avait arrêté 27 nouvelles directives pour améliorer le fonctionnement du système éducatif. Mais le bilan des engagements antérieurs fait apparaître un recul du taux d’exécution : 14 directives sur 32, soit 43,75 %, étaient entièrement réalisées, contre 25 sur 30, soit 83,3 %, lors du précédent bilan. La COSYDEP relève également que seules 11 des 27 nouvelles directives, soit 41 %, comportent une échéance explicite. Pour l’organisation, l’absence de calendrier précis, de responsables clairement identifiés et d’indicateurs de résultats limite les possibilités de suivi et d’évaluation des engagements gouvernementaux. Face à ces constats, la coalition préconise notamment la mise en place d’un registre national des écoles touchées par les inondations, l’accélération de l’assainissement des établissements, la publication de la répartition des enseignants recrutés et le lancement d’un programme de réparation et d’acquisition de tables-bancs. Elle recommande également un plan d’absorption des effectifs en sixième, un accompagnement renforcé des élèves orientés en seconde scientifique et l’activation d’un dispositif national de résilience et de continuité éducative. À plus long terme, l’organisation plaide pour un comité de suivi multipartite des directives, accompagné d’un tableau de bord trimestriel permettant de rendre compte des réalisations, des échéances et des responsabilités. Elle appelle aussi à renforcer le dialogue entre le gouvernement, les syndicats, les parents d’élèves et les organisations de la société civile. Au terme de son analyse, la COSYDEP pose ainsi la question de l’effectivité des politiques éducatives. Pour la coalition, le véritable enjeu ne se limite plus à faire démarrer les cours à la date prévue, mais consiste à garantir, tout au long de l’année, la présence des enseignants, la disponibilité des équipements, la sécurité des établissements et la continuité des apprentissages. Autant de conditions indispensables pour que l’ambition d’une école inclusive, résiliente et performante se traduise effectivement dans le quotidien des élèves. C.T.N
