items.title: Björkegren targets six points as Black Stars prepare for second Somalia clash
items.description: Black Stars interim coach Kim Lars Björkegren says his immediate priority is to secure maximum points from Ghana’s two AFCON qualifying matches as he prepares for his second against Somalia. Ghana beat Somalia 2-0 in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Thursday, with Björkegren now targeting another victory in the return fixture to complete a six-point haul. The Swedish coach admitted that his limited time with the squad has presented some challenges but believes the opening victory has helped create a positive atmosphere within the team. “It’s not so much time that we’ve had together, so it’s a little bit special to come in. With a new group, new staff but the players are relaxed of course it helps to win a game. “Of course, there are areas we have to improve.” Björkegren said his technical team had analysed their opponents and identified areas Ghana must address ahead of the next encounter. “We have watched the videos, and we think we have a clear picture of what we have to do. It is even better to win the game tomorrow. “The most important thing is to make sure that we take six points in this camp. “But I think if we talk too much about how we want to win the game, then maybe we dont. I do think the most important thing is to start strongly, to take our chances, and then maybe we can think about scoring 3 goals or more.” The coach also acknowledged that a victory could significantly change the team’s fortunes but stressed the need for consistency as he continues to assess the squad. “It’s difficult to say in football. Sometimes, a win can build you up fierce and change everything. You can win a game, and things can change very fast. I think we need to stabilise, and there are things that are not my responsibility.” Despite Ghana’s recent struggles, Björkegren remains optimistic about the quality within the squad and believes the Black Stars have the potential to compete for the continental title if they qualify for the 2027 AFCON. “The potential in the group is huge and so high, and I think if we qualify for the AFCON? we can go all the way. But it’s so hard to do, and hopefully, we can win tomorrow to make it six points and get back on track.” He added that the players’ motivation and determination to win back the confidence of supporters have impressed him since taking charge. “I believe a lot in this group. I can feel the good energy, I can feel they are motivated, how hungry they are to show thr fans how good they are and I am pretty show we will see that tomorrow and take it from there.”

items.title: FC AshantiGold ‘04 claim a hard-fought 1-0 home victory over Karela United
items.description: FC AshantiGold ‘04 secured a 1-0 win over Karela United in their Matchday 11 fixture of the Ghana Premier League at the Lens Clay Stadium in Obuasi on Sunday, November 15. After being forced to settle for a goalless draw against Young Apostles last week, the Miners made a strong comeback in this game . After a goalless first 45 minutes, Captain Kojo Twumasi broke the deadlock by scoring the decisive goal in the 89th minute. FC Ashanti Gold ‘04 held firm in the final stretch, preventing Karela United from finding an equalizer. Karela United will need to regroup, analyze their performance, and aim for a victory in their next game after losing 11 straight away matches since February’s victory over Dreams FC. The defeat leaves them on 11 points, sitting in the 14th place. This home victory provides a much-needed boost for FC Ashanti Gold ‘04, who move up to the sixth position with 18 points. The Obuasi- based side are now unbeaten in 21 straight home matches. With 16 wins and 5 draws, Miners remain focused on their ambition to win the league title by the end of the season.

items.title: Simandou Mining Summit : la Guinée rassure et ouvre de nouvelles perspectives aux investisseurs
items.description: Ouvert le 11 novembre 2026 sur l’île de Kassa, le Simandou Mining Summit adresse une invitation claire aux investisseurs : prendre part à la transformation d’un pays déterminé à faire de ses ressources minières le moteur d’une économie diversifiée. Industrie, énergie, agriculture, infrastructures et services constituent les principaux domaines de cette ambition, avec une volonté affirmée de développer des partenariats durables et créateurs de valeur. En effet, la Guinée entend ouvrir un nouveau chapitre de son développement. À l’occasion de cette 1ere édition, le Président de la République, S. E. Mamadi Doumbouya, a présenté une vision qui dépasse l’exploitation du minerai de fer : bâtir, avec les acteurs nationaux et les partenaires internationaux, une économie productive, compétitive et créatrice d’emplois. Cette orientation donne au programme Simandou 2040 toute sa portée stratégique : transformer les richesses du sous-sol en investissements productifs et en progrès durables pour les populations. Dans le prolongement de cette vision, les échanges du 12 novembre 2026, ont placé les réformes, la compétitivité et la confiance au cœur des discussions. M. Djiba Diakité, Ministre Directeur de Cabinet de la Présidence et Président du Comité stratégique de Simandou, a réaffirmé l’ambition de transformation nationale portée par Simandou 2040. Les interventions ont également souligné le rôle déterminant des institutions, de la réalisation des infrastructures et de la gestion à long terme des revenus miniers, notamment à travers la réflexion sur le fonds souverain. Pour les investisseurs, cette orientation ouvre des perspectives qui dépassent largement le secteur extractif. Si une grande exploitation minière génère des besoins en équipements, en infrastructures et en services, une stratégie nationale de transformation élargit davantage les possibilités d’investissement. Elle favorise l’émergence de projets industriels, de partenariats technologiques et d’entreprises capables d’accompagner les mutations de l’économie guinéenne. À cet égard, M. Namory Camara, Directeur général de l’Agence guinéenne de développement, a présenté, lors de l’ouverture, un programme prévoyant plus de 200 milliards de dollars d’investissements sur 15 ans, avec une contribution attendue des capitaux privés de 40 %. Cette ambition de mobilisation financière, dont la concrétisation reposera sur la structuration et l’exécution des projets, traduit la place centrale accordée aux investisseurs. Elle dessine un vaste champ de participation dans l’énergie, les transports, l’agriculture, l’industrie, la santé et l’éducation. Au-delà de ces montants, la Guinée invite ainsi les entreprises à explorer des marchés complémentaires, reliés par les besoins d’une économie en transformation. La maintenance industrielle, la logistique, la transformation agricole, les solutions numériques et la formation technique représentent autant de possibilités à examiner. Pour les entreprises disposant d’une expertise reconnue, de capacités de financement et de partenaires locaux solides, la dynamique Simandou peut constituer un point d’entrée vers une implantation durable. Dans cette perspective, les opérateurs internationaux ont intérêt à identifier les besoins prioritaires, à nouer des alliances avec les entreprises nationales et à investir dans les compétences. De tels partenariats peuvent conjuguer performance économique, transfert de savoir-faire et création d’emplois, tout en renforçant les capacités du tissu entrepreneurial guinéen. Toutefois, la conversion de ces perspectives en investissements durables repose sur des conditions concrètes : des études de qualité, un cadre contractuel lisible, une énergie disponible et compétitive, ainsi que le respect des exigences environnementales et sociales. Ces facteurs sont essentiels pour structurer des projets viables et établir une confiance durable entre l’État, les entreprises et les populations. C’est précisément dans cette logique que s’inscrit le message du Président de la République : la Guinée ne tend pas la main ; elle ouvre ses bras aux investisseurs crédibles, désireux de construire des partenariats mutuellement bénéfiques. L’ambition affichée est de leur offrir un environnement fondé sur la stabilité politique et sociale, la prévisibilité juridique et fiscale, la bonne gouvernance et la lutte contre la corruption. La traduction de ces engagements en actes constitue un levier déterminant pour conforter la confiance et sécuriser les investissements. Dès lors, le Simandou Mining Summit offre une occasion de passer de la reconnaissance du potentiel guinéen à la structuration de projets concrets. Pour les entrepreneurs, les industriels et les financiers, le moment est propice à l’examen des possibilités d’implantation, à la construction de partenariats équilibrés et à la préparation d’investissements répondant aux besoins du pays. Avec Simandou 2040, la Guinée propose un horizon de développement à long terme et une place aux capitaux privés. Aux investisseurs de saisir cette ouverture en apportant financements, technologies et savoir-faire. Investir en Guinée aujourd’hui, c’est se positionner au cœur d’une transformation économique ambitieuse et contribuer à bâtir un pôle de création de valeur en Afrique de l’Ouest. Ibrahima Kalil Keita Directeur Général des Projets Miniers

items.description: TEHRAN – Michel DeGraff, a Haitian-born linguist and professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), has spent three decades examining the relationship between language, power and social justice. His academic work focuses on how language can reinforce social hierarchies and systems of domination, as well as how mother tongues can become instruments of resistance and liberation. His latest book, Our Own Language: Harnessing the Power of Kreyòl and Other Mother Tongues for Education and Liberation, explores these themes through the experience of Haitian Creole and other minoritized languages.

items.title: Mfantsipim School and the founding of Ghana National College – Egbert Faibille Jnr writes
items.description: On the occasion of the 150th Anniversary of Mfantsipim School, it is imperative that we share one significant impact of that School on the independence struggle of the Gold Coast. The record stands that in the wake of the Christiansborg Cross-Roads Shootings on 28th February, 1948, then Gold Coast Governor, Gerald Creasy, ordered a crackdown. That resulted in the arrests of 5 of the Big Six- J.B. Danquah, Ako Adjei, Edward Akufo-Addo, William Ofori Atta, and Emmanuel Obetsebi Lamptey in Accra on suspicion of complicity in the protest march of the ex-servicemen. They were arrested in the immediate aftermath of the disturbances and detained. The other member of the United Gold Coast Convention’s (UGCC) Working Committee, Kwame Nkrumah, was initially fortunate to escape arrest because he had been requested by the others named above to rush to the UGCC’s Saltpond offices to secure it and their documents. Kwame Nkrumah proceeded to Saltpond and, after carrying out the tasks assigned to him, went into hiding in Cape Coast. The Colonial Police took almost 14 days to locate Kwame Nkrumah to arrest him. Pursuant to a Removal Order under the hand of Governor Gerald Creasy dated 12th March, 1948, Kwame Nkrumah was arrested in Cape Coast on that same day. As fate would have it, Kwame Nkrumah was with his then Private Secretary, Saki Scheck, an alumnus of Mfantsipim School at the time of his arrest. With Nkrumah arrested, MOBA Saki Scheck set a scheme in operation when he chanced upon some students of Mfantsipim School in Cape Coast in the immediate aftermath and recounted to them the arrest. Saki Scheck also requested the Mfantsipim students to accompany him to Mfantsipim School to sensitise the students about the arrests of the Big Six. At Mfantsipim School, a student gathering was called for Saki Scheck, who seized the moment to ginger the students to boycott classes and to petition the Colonial government for the immediate release of the Big Six. That Petition was effectively written. From Mfantsipim, Saki Scheck moved to St. Augustine’s College and Adisadel College respectively to undertake the same sensitisation campaign. FindSchools With that, boys and some teachers from the three all-boys schools in Cape Coast embarked on a strike dubbed ‘political’ to demand the release of the Big Six. The strike lasted from 13th March to 20th March, 1948. Mfanstipim School was thus the nerve centre of the strike action. The Colonial government acted swiftly by closing down the three schools. Further, a Conference on the Cape Coast Secondary Schools was called to investigate the strike action and make recommendations. In the end, some 150 boys were expelled for their joint roles in the strike action. Also expelled were four teachers, one of whom was Henry Werner Aryee Kofi Sackeyfio of Mfantsipim School. FindSchools On the release of the Big Six, Kwame Nkrumah seized the opportunity to found Ghana National College on 16th July, 1948 for the dismissed students. On such an occasion, and as a proud alumnus of Ghana National College, I salute Mfantsipim School for its stance in March 1948 and the outcome in July 1948 being the founding of my alma mater. Ghana National College today stands as a nationalist school and the Gold Coast’s defiant response to colonialism. Mfantsipim is the oldest secondary school in Ghana, and Ghana National College is the only school that bore the name ‘Ghana’ almost nine years before the Gold Coast attained independence and assumed the name Ghana. FindSchools Congratulations to Mfantsipim School! Floreat! Mfantsipim! GTO We Care The author is Egbert Faibille Jnr is former President of the Ghana National College Old Students Association.

items.title: Jospong, ISA deepen talks on solar energy, green jobs and climate-smart agriculture
items.description: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) has presented a comprehensive solarisation roadmap to the Jospong Group of Companies (JGC) at the ongoing 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, paving the way for a proposed strategic partnership to accelerate renewable energy deployment, promote green investments and strengthen Africa’s transition towards carbon neutrality. The proposed collaboration seeks to leverage the technical expertise and financing opportunities of the ISA alongside Jospong Group’s extensive operational presence across Africa to develop sustainable solar energy solutions for industrial operations, agriculture and communities. Presenting the roadmap, the Director-General of the International Solar Alliance, Mr Ashish Khanna, emphasised the urgent need to address Africa’s energy access challenges through innovative financing, strategic partnerships, technology transfer and local capacity development. He noted that approximately 600 million Africans still lack access to electricity, despite the continent’s enormous renewable energy potential. Africa, he indicated, accounts for only about 1% of installed global solar photovoltaic capacity, while receiving approximately US$9 billion of the US$521 billion invested in renewable energy globally in 2024. These disparities, he explained, demonstrate the need for stronger partnerships between governments, development institutions and private sector operators to unlock Africa’s solar energy potential. The ISA, an intergovernmental organisation comprising 116 member and signatory countries, is pursuing an ambitious target of mobilising US$1 trillion in solar investments by 2030 under its implementation-driven agenda. Four Strategic Areas of Collaboration The proposed ISA-Jospong partnership focuses on four major areas designed to accelerate solar energy adoption and sustainable development across Africa. The first component involves establishing a dedicated Solar Academy to equip young Africans with practical skills in solar technology, installation, maintenance and renewable energy systems. The initiative is expected to promote technical expertise, create green employment opportunities and develop a skilled workforce capable of supporting Africa’s expanding renewable energy sector. The second component seeks to unlock climate-smart agricultural financing to support the deployment of solar-powered irrigation pumps, particularly for smallholder farmers. The initiative would help reduce dependence on conventional energy sources, improve agricultural productivity and strengthen food security. The ISA has identified solar-powered irrigation as a major opportunity for Africa, where only about 4% of cultivated land is irrigated, compared with 37% in Asia and 14% in Latin America. The third component focuses on facilitating the transfer of modern solar technologies, technical knowledge and international best practices to strengthen local expertise and support renewable energy innovation. This would enable Jospong and other African institutions to adopt cost-effective solar solutions while building the technical capacity required for sustainable operations. A major highlight of the proposed partnership is the solarisation of Jospong Group’s 36 waste treatment plants in Ghana, which would serve as a flagship project for subsequent expansion into other African markets. The initiative forms part of Jospong’s broader green transition strategy, which includes plans to convert approximately 1,000 waste collection trucks from diesel to electric power, supported by solar mini-grids, charging stations and energy storage infrastructure. The proposed solarisation programme is expected to reduce operational dependence on fossil fuels, improve energy security and lower the carbon footprint of the Group’s waste management operations. Jospong Reaffirms Commitment to Improving Energy Management Speaking during the engagement, the General Manager of the Jospong Green Transition Office, Dr Ing. Glenn Kwabenah Gyimah, welcomed the roadmap and reaffirmed the Group’s readiness to work with the International Solar Alliance to advance renewable energy investments across Africa. “Jospong stands ready to begin with solarising our 36 plants in Ghana and to extend this model to our Africa projects. This reflects our strong commitment to low-carbon project development and to minimising the footprint of our products and services as we drive towards our carbon neutrality agenda,” he stated. Dr Gyimah emphasised that the proposed partnership represents a significant opportunity to integrate renewable energy into Jospong’s operations while supporting Africa’s wider climate action and sustainable development objectives. He noted that the Group’s growing investments in green technologies, waste recovery, recycling and sustainable infrastructure provide a strong foundation for the adoption of solar-powered industrial systems. Jospong’s green transition efforts have also attracted international recognition through carbon financing initiatives. At COP28, the Group secured Swiss Government authorisation for internationally transferred mitigation outcomes from its composting facilities, with an estimated value of US$20 million by 2030. The initiative is expected to support further investments in sustainable infrastructure and community development. Expanding Renewable Energy Solutions Across Africa The proposed collaboration is expected to support Jospong’s expanding environmental services and infrastructure operations in African countries, including Nigeria, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Guinea and Liberia. It also aligns with the ISA’s Country Partnership Framework, through which the alliance works with participating countries to accelerate solar investments and strengthen institutional capacity. Ghana signed its Country Partnership Framework with the ISA in September 2025, identifying solar rooftops, community mini-grids, agricultural applications and capacity development as priority areas. The engagement at COP31 therefore presents an opportunity to translate these commitments into practical private sector-led projects with measurable environmental, social and economic benefits. With Africa facing persistent electricity access challenges despite its abundant solar resources, the proposed ISA-Jospong partnership could provide a replicable model for integrating renewable energy into industrial operations, municipal services and agricultural development. For the Jospong Group, the roadmap represents another significant step towards achieving its carbon neutrality ambitions while contributing to Africa’s clean energy transition through innovation, strategic partnerships and sustainable investments.

items.title: Jospong calls for increased private investment in climate-resilient waste infrastructure
items.description: The Jospong Group of Companies has called for increased private sector investment in waste management infrastructure, innovative financing arrangements and technology transfer to help African countries build economies that are resilient to the effects of climate change. The Group’s Chief Investment and Innovation Officer, Dr Noah Gyimah, said inadequate investment in waste management was worsening environmental and public health risks, particularly in African cities where large volumes of municipal waste were disposed of in landfills without prior separation. Speaking as a panellist at a discussion on How the Private Sector Can Help Build Climate-Resilient Economies at the Nepal Pavilion during COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, he said more than 60 per cent of municipal waste generated in many African countries was organic, yet the infrastructure required to separate and process it remained inadequate. He said disposing of mixed waste in landfills contributed to environmental degradation and increased communities’ vulnerability to flooding and disease outbreaks. “Some of the landfills have outlived the population, and then you have all this mix of waste going to the landfills. You can think of flooding,” he said, citing Ghana’s severe flooding in June as an example of the consequences of inadequate investment in the sector. Dr Gyimah said private capital could help bridge the funding gap if investments were structured to generate returns while easing the financial burden on governments. He explained that Jospong mobilised investment through a combination of its own equity, commercial bank financing and support from development finance institutions, backed by public-private partnership arrangements and long-term concession agreements. “Most of these African countries don’t have enough capital to be able to invest in waste management, which has very serious implications for climate change,” he stressed. He said concession agreements spanning 15 to 20 years could provide private investors with the certainty needed to recoup their investments while enabling governments to undertake critical infrastructure projects without bearing the entire financial cost. Making green projects bankable Dr Gyimah identified project development, investment in human capital and research as essential to attracting private capital into climate-related infrastructure. He said investors needed to undertake technical, commercial and financial feasibility studies before presenting projects to banks and other financing institutions. “You need to have the engineers, you need to invest in that, and then when you invest in human capital, you have to invest in research and development,” he said. He cited Jospong’s investment in 38 waste treatment plants across Ghana, with recycling facilities in every region, as an example of the infrastructure development needed to make waste management projects viable. He added that the Group had expanded its operations into 23 other African countries, with active operations in countries including Nigeria, The Gambia and Liberia. According to him, private sector participation should extend beyond immediate financial returns to encompass technology transfer, local skills development, women’s participation and opportunities for young people across the waste management value chain. “Of course, I have a responsibility as a chief investment officer to bring returns to my investor, but I also want to make sure that if I look at that only, then it’s going to be very difficult to build up synergies,” he said. Financing beyond government budgets Dr Gyimah also advocated innovative financing mechanisms that draw on pension funds, insurance companies, commercial banks and other sources of long-term capital to support green infrastructure. He noted that many African economies relied heavily on commercial banks for financing, despite the need to broaden capital markets and attract institutional investors into climate-related projects. He said Ghana’s approach to securing sustainable funding for waste management offered useful lessons for other countries. Under the arrangement he described, a portion of waste-related charges is ring-fenced and placed in an escrow account to support project financing, providing investors with a more predictable revenue stream. He said such mechanisms could improve the bankability and sustainability of projects while reducing dependence on annual government budget allocations. Dr Gyimah further emphasised the importance of adapting technology to local conditions rather than simply transferring systems developed elsewhere. Using Nepal as an example, he said investors would first need to understand the country’s waste composition through proper feasibility studies before determining the most appropriate technology. He also advocated horizontal collaboration with local businesses and industries rather than relying exclusively on vertically integrated investment models. On carbon finance, he disclosed that Jospong had signed an offtake agreement facilitated by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), covering four of its plants in Ghana, with a contract value of approximately US$20 million over four to five years. He said the Group had completed the validation process and was willing to share its technical expertise with Nepal and other countries seeking to develop projects capable of attracting green financing. He urged investors to recognise climate risks and prioritise preparedness rather than wait for disasters to occur. “Don’t wait until the emergency happens; invest to prepare,” he urged. The session also featured Salome Zurabishvili, Executive Director of the UN Global Compact Network Georgia, who highlighted the importance of predictable government policies and incentives in encouraging businesses to invest in climate adaptation. She said effective regulation and government support were essential to strengthening the business case for sustainability, particularly in markets where private sector participation in climate adaptation remained limited.

items.title: GPL 2026/27: Swedru All Blacks held by Berekum Chelsea in goalless draw
items.description: Swedru All Blacks were held to a goalless draw by Berekum Chelsea in their Ghana Premier League encounter after failing to convert their opportunities. The hosts started brightly and came close to breaking the deadlock in the 12th minute when Faisal Charwetey controlled a delivery beautifully on his chest before bringing the ball down to his feet. However, his left-footed effort narrowly missed the target, with the forward coming agonisingly close to giving All Blacks the lead. Neither side could find a breakthrough before the interval, despite four minutes of added time in the first half. The second half followed a similar pattern, with both teams struggling to produce the decisive moment in front of goal. All Blacks made their first changes in the 69th minute, introducing Stephen Baffoe and Samuel Osei Kofi for Charwetey and Zayat Bubakari in an attempt to inject fresh energy into their attack. Prince Arthur was brought on for Latif Blessing in the 82nd minute as the hosts continued their search for a winner. However, Berekum Chelsea held firm to secure a point, with the match ending goalless after 90 minutes. The result leaves both sides with a share of the points after a contest in which neither could find the cutting edge required to claim victory.

items.title: Les féminines de l’AS FAR sacrées championnes d’Afrique
items.description: L'AS FAR a remporté, dimanche, son troisième titre de la Ligue des champions féminine de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF), le deuxième consécutif, en battant le club sud-africain de Mamelodi Sundowns par 3 buts à 1, en finale disputée au stade de l'Autorité du canal de Suez, à Ismaïlia, en Égypte. Déjà sacrées en 2022 et 2025, les joueuses de l'AS FAR ont ainsi ajouté une troisième couronne continentale à leur palmarès, confirmant leur place parmi les grandes formations du football féminin africain. Les Militaires ont ouvert le score à la 23e minute par l'intermédiaire d'Imane Touriss, auteure d'une frappe précise à l'entrée de la surface de réparation, avant que Tholakele ne rétablisse l'égalité pour Mamelodi Sundowns deux minutes plus tard. À la 37e minute, Hiba El Youssfi a redonné l'avantage à la formation marocaine grâce à une frappe déviée par une défenseure sud-africaine. En seconde période, Imane Touriss a inscrit son deuxième but personnel et le troisième de l'AS FAR à la 77e minute, à la suite d'une passe décisive de Fatima Tagnaout, scellant ainsi la victoire du club marocain. La rencontre s'est déroulée en présence notamment de l'ambassadeur du Royaume du Maroc en Égypte, Mohamed Aït Ouali, et du président de la CAF, Patrice Motsepe. L'AS FAR avait décroché son billet pour la finale en s'imposant face au club camerounais de Lekié Football (1-0), tandis que Mamelodi Sundowns avait éliminé la formation ougandaise de Kawempe Muslim Ladies (4-1). Lors de la phase de groupes, les représentantes du Maroc avaient terminé en tête du groupe B avec six points, après deux victoires face à l'AS Bamako du Mali (6-0) et Ampem Darkoa du Ghana (2-0), contre une défaite lors de leur entrée en lice face à Kawempe Muslim Ladies (2-3). La troisième place de cette édition est revenue à Lekié Football, vainqueur samedi de Kawempe Muslim Ladies sur le score de 5 buts à 0. Grâce à ce sacre, l'AS FAR s'est qualifiée pour le deuxième tour des éliminatoires de la Coupe du monde féminine des clubs 2027, où elle affrontera en décembre prochain la formation nord-coréenne de Naegohyang. Le club marocain empochera également une prime de 600.000 dollars au titre de sa victoire finale, tandis que Mamelodi Sundowns percevra 400.000 dollars en tant que finaliste. The post Les féminines de l’AS FAR sacrées championnes d’Afrique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Spéculation et hausse des prix : Tebboune brandit des mesures encore plus sévères
items.description: Le président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune a de nouveau haussé le ton contre la spéculation qui cause des pénuries et des hausses des prix de certains produits de large consommation. Si toutes les mesures dissuasives ne suffisent pas, d’autres lois seront promulguées contre les spéculateurs , a mis en garde le chef de l’État à l’ouverture de l’année judiciaire 2026-2027, ce dimanche 15 novembre au siège de la Cour suprême à Alger. Tebboune : “ La majorité honnête souffre face à une minorité corrompue ” Dans son discours, le président a appelé les magistrats à s'adapter à la période que traverse l’Algérie, marquée par “ la prolifération de la cupidité et de l’enrichissement illicite ”, ainsi que par des “ comportements contraires à la morale ” qui “ menacent le tissu social ”. “ La majorité honnête souffre face à une minorité corrompue ”, a-t-il dénoncé, et c'est pourquoi, a-t-il poursuivi, ” le pouvoir judiciaire doit jouer son rôle essentiel pour mettre fin à cette hégémonie ”. “La protection des classes vulnérables et moyennes est un devoir envers les martyrs” L’économie algérienne, a indiqué le président Tebboune, s’oriente vers une libéralisation totale “ tout en tenant compte du caractère social de l’État ”, car “ la protection des classes vulnérables et moyennes est un devoir envers les martyrs ”. “ C’est ce à quoi nous nous employons ”, a-t-il assuré, ajoutant qu'il faut parvenir à “ un équilibre entre l’ouverture et un contrôle rigoureux de l’économie ”. Néanmoins, a-t-il déploré, “ chaque fois que l’État tente de s’ouvrir sur le plan économique, des gangs apparaissent pour tenter de s’imposer au cœur de ces changements ”. “Ils nous combattent en créant artificiellement des pénuries” “ Nous savons qu’ils nous combattent en s’attaquant aux citoyens, en créant artificiellement des pénuries, et à notre jeunesse par la drogue ”, a dénoncé le président de la République. Et lorsque “ la coupe a débordé ”, des mesures ont été prises comme la décision d’ouvrir la prison de Tanezrouft et celle de rétablir la peine de mort. Abdelmadjid Tebboune a brandi la menace de mesures encore plus drastiques si ces pratiques ne cessent pas. Si ça continue, il y aura de “ nouvelles lois plus strictes ” “ Nous serons contraints de trouver d’autres solutions, et ils n’auront qu’à s’en prendre à eux-mêmes (…) Nous adopterons de nouvelles lois plus strictes pour mettre un terme à certaines pratiques néfastes qui portent atteinte aux Algériens et à leur pouvoir d’achat ”, a-t-il mis en garde. Le président a en outre signifié devant les magistrats qu’il n’y a pas de place en Algérie pour “ les pratiques qui prévalaient à l’époque de la Issaba, telles que le mépris de la loi ou l’abus de pouvoir ”. . Abdelmadjid Tebboune a dit apprécier hautement la lutte menée par la justice contre la corruption et exprimé sa satisfaction des “ avancées réalisées ensemble dans le cadre des réformes ”, tout en se félicitant du fait que la législation algérienne soit un “ exemple pour de nombreux pays ”. L’article Spéculation et hausse des prix : Tebboune brandit des mesures encore plus sévères est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: L'OTAN réduit le nombre de ses sommets et réunions à cause des crises internes et des divergences
items.description: L'OTAN reduit le nombre de ses reunions dans un contexte de divergences internes sur les questions du financement de la defense, du conflit en Ukraine et de la situation en Iran, a rapporte l'Associated Press (AP) ce 15 novembre, citant un entretien avec le secretaire general de l'Alliance, Mark Rutte, et des representants des pays membres. Ainsi, le sommet initialement prevu en 2027 en Albanie n'aura pas lieu. Pendant environ 15 ans, ces reunions se sont tenues pratiquement chaque annee, alors qu'auparavant, l'Alliance reunissait generalement les chefs d'etat et de gouvernement tous les deux ans. Selon l'agence de presse, cette reduction concernera egalement les reunions des ministres de la Defense et des Affaires etrangeres. Ainsi, en octobre dernier, les ministres de la Defense des pays de l'Alliance ne se sont pas reunis, et aucun sommet de ce type n'est prevu en octobre 2027. Les ministres des Affaires etrangeres ne tiendront quant a eux qu'une seule reunion prevue l'annee prochaine, au lieu de deux. L'Alliance justifie ces changements par un « ensemble de mesures de reorganisation ». L'AP a note que certains pays membres de l'OTAN s'etaient opposes a la tenue du sommet en Albanie en raison des depenses militaires de ce pays, jugees insuffisantes a leurs yeux. En 2026, Tirana devrait consacrer 2,15 % de son PIB a la defense, alors que les allies se sont fixe pour objectif d'augmenter les depenses militaires de base a 3,5 % du PIB d'ici 2035 et de consacrer 1,5 % supplementaire aux besoins lies a la defense. Le coût eleve des sommets et les divergences politiques entre les allies ont constitue un facteur supplementaire. Selon l'AP, la preparation de la reunion de La Haye en 2025 a dure environ un an et a coûte pres de 100 millions de dollars. L'agence a egalement rappele que le ministre americain de la Defense, Pete Hegseth, et le secretaire d'etat, Marco Rubio, apres leur entree en fonction, ont regulierement manque les reunions de l'Alliance ou les ont quittees avant la fin. Le 14 novembre, la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, a critique l'OTAN pour avoir compromis la securite du Vieux Continent. Elle a compare l'Alliance a une « dent malade » qui affaiblit le systeme immunitaire de l'Europe, soulignant que « sans ce role que l'OTAN a joue et continue de jouer, il y aurait sans doute bien plus de securite en Europe ».

items.title: Amoakohene calls for review of NAIMOS operations over Manso Keniago deaths
items.description: Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene has called for a review of the operations of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), warning that its approach to the fight against illegal mining could affect the political fortunes of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). He said the government needed to reassess its anti-galamsey strategy following the deaths recorded during a confrontation between NAIMOS personnel and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region. In a Facebook post on Saturday, November 14, 2026, Dr Amoakohene accused some political actors of encouraging the use of lethal force in anti-illegal mining operations and subsequently using the resulting deaths for political gain. “They will push you to fight galamsey with lethal force, then turn around to make political gains out of it. These are the same people who are calling for a state of emergency,” he said. His comments followed calls by the New Patriotic Party’s Director of Communications, Miracles Aboagye, for the government to account for the six deaths reported during the Manso Keniago confrontation. Mr Aboagye had called for a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding each death, arguing that the victims should not automatically be classified as illegal miners or members of a group that confronted the task force. Dr Amoakohene said NAIMOS needed to review its operational approach to prevent the anti-galamsey campaign from becoming a political liability for the NDC. “NAIMOS and their operations must be reviewed before they send NDC back to opposition,” he said. The Regional Minister also questioned calls for the government to adopt a more forceful approach to tackling illegal mining, including demands for a state of emergency. He said he was increasingly agreeing with concerns previously expressed by former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia’s running mate, Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh (NAPO), and Dr Ayew Afriyie about the government’s handling of the anti-galamsey campaign. “I am beginning to agree with NAPO and Dr Ayew on their remarks on the fight against illegal mining,” he said, inviting social media users to share a video of the remarks in the comments section of his post. The Manso Keniago confrontation occurred on November 11, 2026, when NAIMOS personnel encountered resistance while transporting excavators seized during an anti-illegal mining operation. NAIMOS has maintained that its personnel acted in self-defence after encountering an armed group attempting to obstruct the movement of the equipment. Residents and traditional authorities have disputed aspects of the Secretariat’s account. Reports indicated that six people had died and 15 others were injured. The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has also announced an investigation into the incident, although its initial statement cited four deaths and 15 injuries.

items.title: GB police register case as PPP protests alleged malpractice in Diamer repolling
items.description: GILGIT: Re-polling was held at three polling stations in Gilgit-Baltistan’s GBA-16 (Diamer-II) on Sunday, with PPP staging protests in Diamer’s Chilas, as well as Gilgit, against alleged electoral malpractice by the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP). PPP’s Attaullah Shah and IPP’s Imam Malik are the main contenders vying for the seat in the partial repolling, held after an election tribunal accepted Malik’s plea and suspended Shah’s assembly membership. The electoral process began at 8am and continued until 5pm, with voters present within the polling station premises at that time allowed to cast their votes. A total of 2,780 registered voters were eligible. However, after polling concluded, supporters of Shah took to the streets in Diamer district’s Chilas and Gilgit against the alleged removal of ballot boxes from a women’s polling station in Thore Valley. Protesters block Shahrah Quaid-i-Azam near GB Assembly in Gilgit by burning tyres, on Nov 15, 2026. — Jamil Nagri In a statement, the GB Police spokesperson said legal action has been initiated against those who “took away polling material” from the Wara polling station, and a first information report (FIR) under terrorism charges has been registered. The case invoked sections 34 (common intention), 147 (punishment for rioting), 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence), 186 (obstructing public servant), 353 (criminal force to deter public servant from duty) and 392 (punishment for robbery) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), as well as sections 6 and 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA). “The situation is peaceful in the remaining two polling stations,” the police statement affirmed. It warned that strict action under the law will be taken against those who take the law into their hands and block the highways, noting that some of those were already wanted by the police. When contacted, GB Chief Election Commissioner Raja Shahbaz Khan told Dawn that an investigation was under way into the allegations. He noted that foolproof security was provided at the stations, urging people not to take the law into their hands. The election commissioner affirmed that the matter will be resolved. The PPP supporters staged demonstrations on the Karakoram Highway near Chilas, as well as outside the GB Assembly hall in Gilgit, and vowed not to let the public mandate be stolen. Outside the assembly, demonstrators burnt tyres to block the road. One of the protesters, Rehman Deralo, claimed that Malik and others accompanying him entered a polling station and took away ballot boxes and other polling material. PPP workers also staged a protest at Gilgit’s Etihad Chowk, chanting slogans and burning tyres to block the routes. Imtiaz Gilgiti from People’s Youth Organisation, the PPP’s youth wing, said Shah had secured votes from the rival candidate’s hometown and therefore, Malik allegedly stole ballot boxes. Addressing protesters in Gilgit, local PPP leader Shahzad Agha claimed Shah was winning in the polls, but his opponent violated the law and stole the ballot boxes. The former GB minister also termed it negligence by the relevant administration and polling security. “Even if re-polling is conducted 10 times in Diamer, Attaullah will emerge victorious,” Agha contended. Earlier during the day, a source told Dawn that IPP’s Malik had allegedly slapped Polling Officer Dr Maria at the Sarai polling station, adding that the overall polling process remained largely peaceful despite minor unpleasant incidents. Electoral dispute Among the two candidates, Malik had contested the June elections in Gilgit-Baltistan as an independent candidate, but had later joined the IPP. Initially, the Election Commission had declared him the returned candidate for GBA-16 (Diamer-II), but his membership was suspended in September after Shah filed a petition before an election tribunal. The plea contended that the returning officer (RO) had issued Form-49 without counting the postal ballots. In its order on Sept 11, the tribunal directed the relevant RO to complete the verification and counting of postal ballot papers by September 16 and, meanwhile, suspended Malik’s membership. Subsequently, the counting and verification of postal ballots for GBA-16 (Diamer-II) was held and Shah was declared the winner on Sept 14. According to the revi­sed consolidated results issued by the GB Election Com­mission on Form-49, Shah secured 6,618 votes, defeating Malik by a margin of just 13 votes. But then, Malik had challenged the tribunal’s decision before the GB Supreme Appellate Court. On Sept 19, the appellate court dismissed his appeal against the suspension of his membership and upheld the tribunal’s decision declaring Shah the returned candidate. Malik later again challenged the results at three polling stations and petitioned the election tribunal to order re-polling. The tribunal accepted his plea and suspended Shah’s membership and directed the chief election commissioner to conduct re-polling at the three polling stations within 12 days of Nov 6.

items.title: Guinée : Plus de 1 500 orpailleurs illégaux graciés et reconduits à la frontière à Kourémalé
items.description: Ce dimanche 15 novembre 2026, un long convoi transportant 1 557 orpailleurs clandestins de nationalités multiples a franchi le poste frontalière de Kourémalé, selon une publication de la Direction de l’Information et des Relations publiques des Armées (DIRPA. Interpellés dans des sites miniers puis élargis à la suite d'une grâce, ces ressortissants étrangers ont été raccompagnés dans leur pays d'origine dans le cadre d'une opération de souveraineté hautement sécurisée. ​Parti de Kankan, le convoi officiel s'est ébranlé sur les routes guinéennes pour mener à bien cette opération de refoulement encadrée. « Arrêtés dans les sites miniers, jugés à Kourémalé puis élargis, ces orpailleurs illégaux ont été reconduits à la frontière dans le cadre d’un dispositif d’envergure. Au sol, le cortège s’est révélé impressionnant, tandis que dans les airs, des moyens aériens ont appuyé le mouvement. Une telle configuration témoigne de la détermination des autorités guinéennes à faire respecter la loi tout en maîtrisant l’opération jusqu’à son terme », souligne la DIRPA . Composé de pas moins de 44 véhicules, le cortège terrestre a bénéficié d'un appui aérien significatif, illustrant la fermeté et la rigueur des autorités guinéennes. ​Selon le ministère guinéenne de la Défense nationale, la transition s'est déroulée dans un climat d'ordre et de concorde. Le consulat du Burkina Faso à Conakry a activement pris part au trajet, tandis que les autorités maliennes et burkinabè étaient fortement mobilisées sur place à Kourémalé pour réceptionner leurs ressortissants. « La remise s’est effectuée dans l’ordre et la dignité, sans chaos ni débordement » . ​Au-delà de la stricte application de la loi, la séquence a également été marquée par des scènes de liesse et de soulagement inattendues. Les 1 557 hommes concernés, bien qu'impliqués dans des activités illicites par le passé, n'ont pas manqué d'exprimer leur profonde reconnaissance envers la clémence du peuple guinéen et des autorités du pays. « La clémence du peuple hospitalier guinéen ainsi que celle du président Mamadi Doumbouya ont été solennellement saluées », a indiqué la DIRPA. ​Les populations locales de Kourémalé ont, de leur côté, accueilli cet épilogue avec bienveillance, multipliant les marques de sympathie et adressant des messages de remerciement au chef de l'État. ​À travers cette opération menée tambour battant, la Guinée démontre une double exigence : une intransigeance absolue contre l'exploitation minière illégale sur son sol, conjuguée à un sens aigu de la retenue, de la dignité et de l'hospitalité dans l'exécution de ses décisions souveraines.

items.title: Vatar, makers of Lagos Life, launches in Ghana
items.description: The makers of Lagos Life are bringing Accra, Kumasi, and Tema into a growing network of interconnected African virtual worlds. Vatar, the African gaming company behind Lagos Life, today announced its first international expansion into Ghana, launching virtual experiences of Accra, Kumasi and Tema. The expansion comes just six weeks after the launch of Lagos Life, which surpassed 11 million players in its first month, becoming a rapidly growing social gaming experience built around African cities and everyday life. Founded by Nigerian software developer Shalom Rayhamen, Vatar is building a connected world where people can live, work, socialise, own property and explore cities inspired by real places and cultures. With Ghana joining Nigeria, players can now experience six virtual cities across two countries, travelling between them through a shared digital world that brings familiar African experiences into gaming. The Ghana launch marks the next step in Vatar’s ambition to build a global network of culturally authentic virtual cities, beginning with Africa. Shalom built Lagos Life and launched it on 1st October 2026, Nigeria’s Independence Day. As a fan of life-simulation games, she wanted a world where players could live a full virtual life in a city they recognise. Players create a character, find a job, earn and spend virtual money, rent a home, ride public transport and socialise with other players in real time, all from a web browser. The response was immediate, driven by how relatable the game felt. Lagos Life reached one million players in four days, and within its first month it grew beyond Lagos to include Abuja and Port Harcourt. Shalom co-founded Vatar in October 2026 with Owen Rayhamen, Chief Product Officer, Anderson Oriahi, Chief Operating Officer, and Shantel Oriahi, Chief Financial Officer, to grow the game into a network of social worlds based on real cities. Ahead of the launch, Shalom and the Vatar team travelled to Ghana to meet partners and leaders in the country’s gaming and creative industries, including Kwesi Hayford, President of the Esports Association, Ghana (EAG), to shape the expansion plans with them. The aim is a Ghana experience built with Ghanaians, reflecting the everyday life, places and culture of each city. As with Lagos Life, each city is built to feel real. Players can shop at Accra Mall, browse Kejetia Market in Kumasi, explore the harbour city of Tema, take city tours and travel internationally. Hayford is an esports leader, creative designer and digital media entrepreneur with more than a decade in esports leadership. Under his leadership, EAG launched the Ghana Esports League, the country’s first structured national esports league, and helped start the African Esports Championships with 15 countries. He also founded PlayArena, KiddieEsports and Ruutz Esports. “Lagos Life was born from my love for The Sims growing up. The game was always set in American cities, and while I enjoyed it, it never felt native to me. I didn’t feel seen or represented. My vision with Vatar is to build worlds from Africa to the world, where every city feels familiar and relatable, and every person feels seen. I want players to see their everyday lives reflected in the game. For Ghana, we have shaped this launch with Ghanaians, and for Ghanaians, we can’t wait for players in Accra, Kumasi and Tema to live their city’s story on Vatar,” said Shalom Rayhamen, Founder and CEO of Vatar. “Africa’s games bridge cultures and build the digital skills that empower our youth. Vatar (Lagos Life) is not just another game; it is a platform to connect, play and win, built in Africa for a global audience and grounded in the excellence Africa can envision,” said Kwesi Hayford, President of the Esports Association, Ghana (EAG). Ghana goes live on Vatar on Sunday, 15 November 2026, at vatar.com. Vatar is free to play in a web browser on a phone or computer, with no download needed, and is also available as Vatar on the Google Play Store and soon to be on the App Store. It is open to players aged 18 and over. Vatar builds social virtual worlds based on real cities, where people live their city’s story: they work, own property, socialise and build a life. Its first world, Lagos Life, launched on 1 October 2026 and, within its first month, expanded beyond Lagos to Abuja and Port Harcourt and passed 11 million players. In November 2026, Vatar launched in Ghana with Accra, Kumasi and Tema. Shalom Rayhamen (Founder and CEO), Owen Rayhamen (Chief Product Officer), Anderson Oriahi (Chief Operating Officer), and Shantel Oriahi (Chief Financial Officer) co-founded Vatar in 2026.

items.title: Amoakohene formally bows out as NDC Ashanti Regional Secretary, touts party’s electoral gains
items.description: Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene has formally ended his tenure as Ashanti Regional Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), following the successful conclusion of the party’s regional executive elections. In a Facebook post announcing his departure, Dr Amoakohene described his service in the position as one of the greatest honours of his life, while reflecting on what he considers significant achievements recorded by the party in the Ashanti Region during his tenure. He said the NDC had made considerable electoral progress in the region, traditionally regarded as a stronghold of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), despite the challenges associated with expanding its political influence there. According to him, the party increased its parliamentary representation in the region from four seats to seven, while also narrowing the electoral gap in several other constituencies. He further disclosed that the NDC improved its presidential vote share in the Ashanti Region from approximately 26.5 per cent in the 2020 general election to more than 34 per cent in 2024. Dr Amoakohene described the gains as achievements that many had previously considered impossible, crediting the collective efforts of party members and supporters. “Together, we achieved what many said was impossible in Ashanti,” he said. Beyond the electoral gains, he highlighted the completion of the Ashanti Regional Party Secretariat as another major achievement during his tenure. He acknowledged the contributions of party members and predecessors who initiated the project, expressing gratitude for the opportunity to complete an initiative started by earlier generations of NDC leadership. “We were privileged to finish what they began,” he said. Dr Amoakohene also expressed appreciation to President John Dramani Mahama and the party’s national executives for their leadership and guidance throughout his period in office. He stressed that the achievements could not be attributed to one individual, acknowledging the contributions of constituency executives, branch and ward executives, the women’s and youth wings, the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN), the Zongo Caucus, party elders, patrons and grassroots supporters. He particularly commended the party’s foot soldiers, whose commitment and organisational efforts, he said, contributed to strengthening the NDC’s presence across the region. As the party transitions to a new regional leadership, Dr Amoakohene urged constituency and regional executives who retained their positions to intensify their efforts and work closely with the incoming leadership. He also offered words of encouragement to those who lost their positions in the elections, assuring them that their contributions and sacrifices would remain part of the party’s progress. “To those who unfortunately lost: you will not be forgotten. Your sacrifice is part of everything we built,” he stated.

items.title: When even your Traffic Fine is a scam!
items.description: By Jimmy Aglah Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, the government decided that Ghanaian motorists had enjoyed too much freedom on the roads. Some drove as though speed limits were recommendations from elderly relatives, deserving respectful consideration but not necessarily obedience. Others regarded traffic lights as Christmas decorations, beautiful to behold but entirely optional. The authorities therefore introduced electronic traffic enforcement, hoping cameras would accomplish what policemen, road signs and decades of public education had struggled to achieve. It was a brilliant idea. Cameras do not accept apologies, recognise party colours or appreciate the significance of a driver’s uncle being a Deputy Minister. They simply record offences and leave the authorities to do the rest. Unfortunately, the Republic’s fraudsters were also watching. And being patriotic citizens with an extraordinary appetite for business opportunities, they apparently decided that government should not enjoy a monopoly over the collection of money from frightened motorists. Thus was born Ghana’s newest potential growth industry: Traffic Fine Entrepreneurship. For years, our enterprising fraudsters concentrated on traditional sectors of the deception economy. They promised unsuspecting citizens foreign visas, miraculous investments, parcels of gold and romantic relationships with wealthy strangers who mysteriously required financial assistance before declaring their undying love. But every industry must innovate or perish. Why promise somebody an inheritance from a dead millionaire in London when you can simply inform him that his Toyota Corolla has offended the Republic? No complicated love story. No inheritance documents. Just a threatening message, an alleged traffic offence and instructions to pay before trouble arrives. The Ghana Police Service warned motorists about fraudulent traffic penalty notices on 4 November 2026, while the Cyber Security Authority followed on 9 November with concerns about fake messages and payment websites. Evidently, some people had discovered that where government establishes a collection system, unofficial competitors may soon arrive with their own invoices. In the Republic of Uncommon Sense, even criminality believes in public-private partnership. Consider the predicament of the ordinary Ghanaian motorist. He leaves home determined to obey every traffic regulation. At the first junction, a taxi overtakes him from the wrong side. At the next, an aboboyaa carrying enough merchandise to establish a branch of Kejetia Market passes him with the confidence of a presidential convoy. Before reaching his destination, three motorcycles have demonstrated that road markings are merely artistic expressions on asphalt. Our gentleman, meanwhile, is doing 50 kilometres per hour, glancing nervously at his speedometer as though it contains the examination results of his firstborn. Then his telephone announces the arrival of a traffic penalty. Ei! He checks the message, his registration number and his memory. Was it yesterday? Last Tuesday? Perhaps the day he accelerated slightly to escape an impatient truck whose driver appeared to believe that brakes were invented for cowards. The message demands payment. But is it genuine? One friend advises him to ignore it. Another warns that failure to pay could lead to prosecution. A third suggests visiting the police station. A fourth, who considers himself an expert in digital governance because he once successfully renewed his passport online, recommends checking the official platform. By the time our motorist finishes his consultations, he has spent enough airtime to finance a small telecommunications company. And he still cannot establish whether he owes the Republic money or whether the Republic’s unofficial business community is attempting to collect a private tax. What a country! Our ancestors warned that when two elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers. In modern Ghana, however, the elephants have discovered mobile money, and the grass is being asked to enter its PIN. The tragedy is that electronic traffic enforcement is not inherently a bad idea. Ghana’s roads have witnessed enough recklessness to convince even the most stubborn optimist that something must change. We cannot continue treating road safety as a seasonal sermon delivered during Christmas and Easter, only to return afterwards to the national sport of overtaking death at dangerous bends. But technology without adequate public education can become an elaborate invitation to confusion. When motorists are uncertain about how official notices are delivered, where penalties should be verified and which payment channels are legitimate, fraudsters need little imagination. They merely dress deception in the respectable clothing of government authority and wait for frightened citizens to open their wallets. As the elders say, when the owner of the house fails to identify his children, the stranger may enter the compound and demand supper. Indeed, perhaps the Republic should introduce a compulsory examination for motorists: Advanced Traffic Fine Authentication. Question One: You receive a message claiming that your vehicle exceeded the speed limit. What should you do? A. Pay immediately before the police arrest your ancestors. B. Forward the message to your family WhatsApp group for collective interpretation. C. Consult your pastor to determine whether the offence is physical or spiritual. D. Verify the notice through the officially authorised channel. Naturally, the correct answer is D. Unfortunately, in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, many citizens may have exhausted A, B and C before discovering D. And therein lies the serious matter beneath the laughter. The success of electronic enforcement depends not merely on detecting wrongdoing but also on public confidence. A genuine penalty must be distinguishable from a fraudulent demand without requiring the investigative resources of EOCO, the patience of Job and the technical expertise of a cybersecurity consultant. Government must make verification simple, publicise authorised payment channels and ensure suspicious notices can be reported without unnecessary bureaucracy. Otherwise, motorists may ignore legitimate penalties because they suspect fraud, while others pay criminals because they fear prosecution. The criminal wins either way. Perhaps the greatest irony is that the Republic has invested in technology to detect motorists exceeding speed limits, only to discover that fraudsters are equally determined to overtake the enforcement system in the race for the motorist’s money. And so, in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, government is pursuing speeding motorists, fraudsters are pursuing frightened motorists, and frightened motorists are pursuing somebody who can explain which pursuit is legitimate. Perhaps the next generation of traffic cameras should be programmed to detect not only speeding vehicles but also speeding fraudsters. For in a country where even a traffic fine can be counterfeit, the only thing travelling faster than the motorist is the criminal’s imagination. And unlike the unfortunate driver, that imagination appears to have no speed limit.

items.title: Musulmans de France : entre le souci du détail et le sens des priorités
items.description: Depuis l’entrée en vigueur des dispositifs de lutte contre le « séparatisme », l’accumulation de mesures administratives visant les institutions musulmanes en France dessine une tendance de fond, qui suscite de nombreuses interrogations : des opérations de contrôle ont été menées, aboutissant à la fermeture de plusieurs mosquées ou salles de prière, à l’expulsion de dizaines d’imams et de prédicateurs, ainsi qu’à la fermeture ou à la dissolution de nombreuses associations culturelles et d’enseignement de la langue arabe. Dans le domaine éducatif, cette pression s’est également traduite par des décisions visant des établissements privés sous contrat, notamment des écoles et lycées musulmans . Des décisions qui fragilisent les structures éducatives, culturelles et cultuelles des musulmans de France Plusieurs établissements scolaires musulmans ont perdu leur contrat d’association avec l’État, fragilisant leur financement public et leur avenir. Cette situation pourrait, à terme, conduire à la fermeture de certaines de ces structures. Si les pouvoirs publics justifient ces mesures par la défense des principes républicains, plusieurs juristes et responsables associatifs alertent sur leurs conséquences pour les structures éducatives, culturelles et cultuelles des musulmans de France. Pourtant, sur les réseaux sociaux notamment, une grande partie des discussions au sein de la communauté musulmane continue de se concentrer sur des questions qui, bien qu’importantes sur le plan individuel, occupent un espace disproportionné : viande halal, la présence d’alcool ou de gélatine dans certains produits, les normes vestimentaires, les horaires de prière ou encore le statut de la musique. Ces sujets alimentent des polémiques interminables, tandis que les véritables enjeux collectifs peinent à susciter la même mobilisation. Ce décalage devrait nous interpeller. D’un côté, des institutions sont fragilisées et des espaces essentiels de transmission disparaissent ; de l’autre, nous consacrons une énergie considérable à des débats relevant souvent de choix personnels, d’interprétations religieuses ou de divergences d’opinions. L’enjeu n’est pas d’éluder ces questions, dont certaines touchent légitimement à la pratique cultuelle, mais de refuser qu’elles monopolisent l’attention au détriment des combats décisifs pour notre avenir collectif. Les véritables enjeux Il ne s’agit nullement d’opposer la foi à l’engagement citoyen, ni de renoncer à nos principes religieux, mais simplement de retrouver le sens des priorités. À quoi bon multiplier les controverses sur les détails du quotidien si nous demeurons incapables de nous mobiliser pour préserver les écoles de nos enfants, défendre nos lieux de culte et soutenir les associations qui assurent la transmission de notre patrimoine spirituel ? Les prescriptions religieuses conservent naturellement toute leur légitimité. Mais elles ne doivent pas occulter des enjeux autrement plus déterminants : la défense des libertés fondamentales, l’éducation de nos jeunes, la pérennité de nos institutions et la structuration de notre tissu associatif. À l'heure où les musulmans de France participent pleinement à la vie économique, sociale et culturelle du pays, défendre leurs droits, préserver leurs structures et faire entendre leur voix ne relève en rien d'un repli communautaire, mais d'une exigence strictement démocratique. Le temps est venu d’opérer un changement de cap : substituer aux controverses stériles une réflexion stratégique exigeante, ancrée dans la solidarité et l’action collective. Un tel sursaut impose de surmonter les divisions, les rivalités et les querelles d’ego qui minent trop souvent la cohésion des initiatives communes. Une communauté ne se construit pas uniquement autour de prescriptions alimentaires ou de controverses théologiques. Elle se construit aussi par ses écoles, ses lieux de culte, ses associations et sa capacité à préparer l’avenir des générations futures. Le véritable enjeu n’est donc pas de moins parler de religion, mais de faire émerger une conscience collective apte à défendre ses droits, protéger ses institutions et tracer des perspectives durables. Car à force de nous épuiser dans des querelles secondaires, nous risquons de déserter les combats essentiels, et de perdre les espaces mêmes qui nous permettent de vivre, de transmettre et d’incarner notre fois. « À l'heure où les musulmans de France participent pleinement à la vie économique, sociale et culturelle du pays, défendre leurs droits, préserver leurs structures et faire entendre leur voix ne relève en rien d'un repli communautaire, mais d'une exigence strictement démocratique. » Azzédine Gaci, recteur de la mosquée de Villeurbanne L’article Musulmans de France : entre le souci du détail et le sens des priorités est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Barrages : le taux de remplissage atteint 66,27 % au Maroc
items.description: La situation hydrique du Maroc connaît une amélioration notable. Le taux de remplissage global des barrages a atteint 66,27 % ce dimanche 15 novembre 2026, pour un volume total stocké de près de 11,28 milliards de mètres cubes, sur une capacité normale de 17,03 milliards de m³. Selon les données officielles du ministère de l’Équipement et de l’Eau, cette progression apparaît particulièrement importante par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente. Au 15 novembre 2025, le taux de remplissage national ne dépassait pas 31,03 %. Le volume des ressources hydriques stockées a ainsi plus que doublé en un an. Les niveaux de remplissage restent toutefois variables selon les bassins hydrauliques. Le Tensift arrive en tête avec un taux de remplissage de 80,37 %, devant Bouregreg (76,53 %) et Sebou (73,84 %). Le bassin de Moulouya affiche pour sa part un taux de 72,45 %, tandis que le Loukkos atteint 72,20 %. Dans les bassins enregistrant des niveaux intermédiaires, le taux de remplissage s’établit à 59,79 % pour Ziz-Ghéris et à 59,60 % pour l’Oum Er-Rbia. Dans les régions du centre et du sud du Royaume, les réserves atteignent 53,02 % dans le bassin du Souss-Massa, contre 39,51 % dans celui du Drâa-Oued Noun. Le barrage Al Wahda à près de 75 % Les principaux barrages du Royaume affichent également des niveaux de remplissage contrastés. Le barrage Al Wahda, situé dans le bassin du Sebou et considéré comme le plus grand du Maroc, affiche un taux de remplissage de 74,98 %, avec un volume stocké estimé à 2,59 milliards de m³. Le barrage Al Massira, deuxième plus grand ouvrage hydraulique du pays et situé dans le bassin de l’Oum Er-Rbia, présente en revanche un taux de remplissage de 41,87 %, pour un volume stocké de 1,11 milliard de m³. D’autres infrastructures stratégiques affichent des niveaux élevés, notamment Bin El Ouidane, à 78,69 %, Idriss Ier, à 71,68 %, et Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah, dans le bassin du Bouregreg, à 71,78 %. Un seul barrage à 100 % Les données quotidiennes font également ressortir un barrage ayant atteint sa capacité maximale. Il s’agit du barrage situé sur l’oued Za, dans le bassin de la Moulouya, dont le taux de remplissage s’établit à 100 %. Sa capacité normale est de 87,92 millions de m³. La situation contraste avec celle observée à la même date en 2025. Plusieurs barrages avaient alors atteint leur capacité maximale, notamment Allal El Fassi, M'Jaa Sebou, Sidi Driss et Aït Massoud. Malgré cette différence, l’évolution globale des réserves témoigne d’une nette amélioration de la situation hydrique nationale. La progression enregistrée cette année apporte ainsi un répit au système hydraulique marocain après plusieurs années marquées par la pression sur les ressources en eau. The post Barrages : le taux de remplissage atteint 66,27 % au Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Mahama urges traditional authorities to strengthen role in promoting peace and social cohesion
items.description: President John Mahama has described traditional authorities as indispensable partners in Ghana’s national development, urging them to strengthen their contribution to peace, social cohesion and community development. He said traditional institutions remained critical to addressing some of the country’s challenges, including unemployment, social inequality, land and chieftaincy disputes, environmental degradation and threats to national security. The President made the remarks in an address delivered on his behalf by the Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, at a ceremony in Sandema in the Upper East Region to mark the 20th anniversary of the passing of the late Nab Dr Ayieta Azantilow. President Mahama said the late traditional ruler demonstrated that traditional leadership must go beyond preserving customs and exercising customary authority to include improving the social and economic conditions of the people. He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to working closely with traditional authorities and other stakeholders to support initiatives aimed at improving living conditions, expanding opportunities for the youth and promoting sustainable development across the country. The President also cautioned the youth against the use of illicit drugs, warning that drug abuse posed a serious threat to their well-being, future prospects and the country’s development. He urged traditional authorities to guide young people towards responsible choices and collaborate with government and other stakeholders to address the problem and protect the younger generation. President Mahama expressed hope that the commemoration would strengthen unity among chiefs and people of the Bulsa Traditional Area and inspire renewed commitment to the development of the area and the Upper East Region. The ceremony also featured the launch of a book in honour of the late traditional ruler, whose nearly 75-year reign was distinguished by contributions to education, healthcare, traditional governance and community development.

items.title: Kvaratskhelia encense Hakimi : « Le meilleur arrière droit de l’histoire »
items.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia n’a pas tari d’éloges à l’égard de son coéquipier au Paris Saint-Germain, Achraf Hakimi. Lors d’un live sur Twitch, l’international géorgien a qualifié le Marocain de « meilleur arrière droit au monde », allant jusqu’à le considérer comme le meilleur arrière droit de l’histoire du football. La séquence est intervenue après un échange téléphonique entre les deux joueurs. Hakimi avait pris des nouvelles de Kvaratskhelia, éloigné des terrains ces dernières semaines en raison d’une grave blessure au ligament croisé antérieur du genou droit. Touché par l’attention de son coéquipier, le Géorgien en a profité pour mettre en avant les qualités du capitaine des Lions de l’Atlas. Au-delà de ses performances sportives, Kvaratskhelia a également insisté sur les qualités humaines de Hakimi, estimant qu’il était difficile de trouver une meilleure personne que lui. « Il n’y en a pas de meilleur » Pour Kvaratskhelia, les qualités de Hakimi dépassent largement son rendement sur le terrain. Le latéral marocain s’est imposé comme l’un des joueurs majeurs du PSG grâce à sa capacité à se projeter, son apport offensif et son activité défensive. Le Géorgien a également profité de son direct pour saluer l’ensemble du groupe parisien, qu’il considère comme exceptionnel, aussi bien sur le plan sportif que dans les relations humaines qui unissent les joueurs en dehors du terrain. Cette sortie intervient quelques jours après la nouvelle démonstration de Hakimi avec le Maroc. Le défenseur parisien a inscrit deux buts lors de la large victoire des Lions de l’Atlas face au Niger, en qualifications pour la Coupe d’Afrique des nations. Une performance qui confirme son influence croissante, aussi bien avec le PSG qu’avec la sélection marocaine. Hakimi, favori pour le Ballon d’Or africain Les déclarations de Kvaratskhelia viennent renforcer la reconnaissance dont bénéficie Hakimi au plus haut niveau. Auteur d’une année 2026 particulièrement remarquée, le Marocain apparaît comme l’un des principaux prétendants au Ballon d’Or africain 2026. Entre ses performances avec le PSG et son rôle déterminant avec les Lions de l’Atlas, Hakimi continue ainsi de s’imposer comme l’un des joueurs marocains les plus en vue sur la scène internationale. The post Kvaratskhelia encense Hakimi : « Le meilleur arrière droit de l’histoire » appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
